Commentary of Tafsir of Surah al-Qalam (Surah 68)

It is a Meccan surah. (Note: the source text states it is Madani; translating as given.)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hija') has already passed at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and that ﴿Nun﴾ is like ﴿Sad﴾ and ﴿Qaf﴾ and similar disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs. The matter has been examined there sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a great fish upon the surging of the vast encompassing water, and it is the bearer of the seven earths, as the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan - that is al-Thawri - narrated to us, Sulayman - that is al-A'mash - narrated to us, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree." So it ran with what would happen from that day until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" and raised the vapour of the water, and from it the sky was split open, and the earth was spread out on the back of the Nun. The Nun then convulsed, and the earth shook, so it was made firm with the mountains, for indeed they boast over the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it similarly from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Likewise it was narrated by Shu'ba, Muhammad ibn Fudayl, and Waki', from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Shu'ba added in his narration: Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Sharik narrated it from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan - or Mujahid - from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar. Ma'mar narrated from al-A'mash that Ibn 'Abbas said... and mentioned it, then recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed the first thing my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, created was the pen. Then He said to it: "Write!" So it wrote what is to occur until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" above the water, then He pressed the earth upon it.

Al-Tabarani has narrated this raised (marfu') as well. He said: Abu Habib - Zayd ibn al-Muhtadi al-Marwazi - narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Taliqani narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the first things Allah created were the pen and the fish. He said to the pen: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Every existing thing until the Day of Resurrection.'" Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ So the "Nun" is the fish, and the "Qalam" is the pen.

Another narration on this: Ibn 'Asakir narrated it from Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He created the 'Nun', which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur - or: what is existing - of deed, or provision, or trace, or term.' So it wrote that until the Day of Resurrection, and that is His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Then He sealed the pen, and it has not spoken until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: 'By My might, I shall perfect you in whomever I love, and I shall diminish you in whomever I hate.'"

Ibn Abi Najih said: Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed him, from Mujahid, who said: It was said: "The Nun is the great fish beneath the seventh earth."

Al-Baghawi and a group of the exegetes mentioned: that upon the back of this fish is a rock whose thickness is like the thickness of the heavens and the earth, and upon its back is a bull having forty thousand horns, and upon its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them. Allah knows best. And it is strange that some of them applied this meaning to the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Isma'il narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas: that 'Abd Allah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madina, so he came to him and asked him about things. He said: "I will ask you about things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise eat? Why does the child resemble its father, and why does the child resemble its mother?" He said: "Jibril informed me of them just now." Ibn Salam said: "He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." He said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise eat, it is the caudate lobe of the fish's liver. As for the child, when the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child resembles the man, and when the woman's water precedes the man's water, she resembles her."

Al-Bukhari narrated it through several chains from Humayd, and Muslim also narrated it. And in it, from the hadith of Thawban, mawla of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), something similar. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Thawban: that a rabbi asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about questions, and among them he said: "What is their gift?" - meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise - He said: "The caudate lobe of the fish's liver." He said: "What is their nourishment after it?" He said: "The bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which used to graze on its edges." He said: "What is their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring therein called Salsabil."

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a tablet of light.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Shabib al-Muktib narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ A tablet of light, and a pen of light, running with what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection." This is mursal and gharib.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that this pen is of light, its length being a hundred years.

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is an inkwell, and the ﴿Qalam﴾ is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatada regarding His saying ﴿Nun﴾, they both said: it is the inkwell.

A raised hadith of extreme strangeness has been narrated on this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created the Nun, which is the inkwell."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, my brother 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Thabit al-Thumali narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah created the Nun - which is the inkwell - and created the pen, and said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection of deed done, whether righteous or wicked, or provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful." Then He bound each thing of that, its affair: its entry into the world, how long its stay therein, and how its exit will be. Then He placed over the servants guardians, and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day from the keepers the deed of that day. When the provision is exhausted, the trace is cut off, and the term has ended, the guardians come to the keepers seeking the deed of that day. The keepers say to them: "We find nothing for your companion with us," so the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: So Ibn 'Abbas said: "Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29]? And is copying anything but from an original?"

* *

As for His saying ﴿By the pen﴾, the apparent meaning is that it is the genus of the pen with which one writes, as in His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾ [al-'Alaq: 3-5]. So it is an oath by Him, exalted be He, and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them by teaching writing, through which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada said: meaning: what they write.

Abu al-Duha said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, i.e., what they do.

al-Suddi said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, meaning the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants.

Others said: rather, what is meant here by the pen is the pen which Allah set running by the decree when He wrote the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They cited in this the hadiths reported concerning the mention of the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Yunus ibn Habib both said: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym al-Sulami narrated to us, from 'Ata' - that is Ibn Abi Rabah - Al-Walid ibn 'Ubada ibn al-Samit narrated to me, who said: My father called me when death came to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: "Write!" It said: "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree [what has been] and what will occur forever."'"

This hadith has been narrated by Imam Ahmad through several chains, from al-Walid ibn 'Ubada, from his father, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with it, and said: hasan sahih gharib. Abu Dawud narrated it in his book "al-Sunna" of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from Ibn Rabah, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla, from Abu Hafsa - whose name is Hubaysh ibn Shurayh al-Habashi al-Shami - from 'Ubada, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tusi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Rabah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, so He commanded it, and it wrote everything." Strange from this route, and they did not transmit it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿By the pen﴾, meaning: that with which the Reminder was written.

* *
His saying, ﴿and what they write﴾, means: what they write, as was mentioned earlier.

* *
His saying, ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾, means: you are not, praise be to God, a madman, as some ignorant people among your folk may say, those who deny the guidance and clear truth you have brought them, and so they attribute madness to you because of it. ﴿Indeed, for you there is a reward never cut off﴾ means: rather, for you there is a great reward and an abundant recompense that does not end and does not perish, for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and for your patience with their harm. The meaning of ﴿never cut off﴾ is: not interrupted, like His saying: ﴿a gift not withdrawn﴾ [Hud: 108], and ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾ [At-Tin: 6], meaning not cut off from them. Mujahid said: ﴿never cut off﴾ means: not counted, and this returns to what we have stated.

* *
His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means, indeed you are upon a tremendous religion [[In A: "upon a tremendous character".]], which is Islam. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said likewise.
'Atiyyah said: upon a tremendous courtesy (adab).
Ma'mar reported from Qatadah: 'A'ishah was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "His character was the Qur'an," meaning she would recite as it is in the Qur'an.
Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah reported from Qatadah concerning His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾: it was mentioned to us that Sa'd [[In A: "A, Sa'id".]] ibn Hisham asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa [[In A: "Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa".]], from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I asked 'A'ishah, and I said: "Inform me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/245).]]
This is a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in full in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah [[Sahih Muslim, no. 746.]], and it will come in Surah Al-Muzzammil, God willing.
Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Al-Hasan, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Al-Musnad (6/216).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Qays ibn Wahb, from a man of the Banu Sawad, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?" I said: "Tell me about that." She said: "I prepared food for him, and Hafsah prepared food for him. I said to my slave-girl: Go, and if she comes with the food and places it before him first, then throw the food down!" She said: "So she came with the food, and the slave-girl turned, and the dish fell and broke, and it was a leather mat [[In H, M, A: "nit'", and the text follows Al-Musnad.]]." She said: "So the Messenger of God gathered it up and said: 'Give it [or: give it, O such-and-such] a dish in place of your dish.'" [Aswad was unsure whether it was "give" in the masculine or feminine form.] She said: "And he said nothing."
Ibn Jarir said: 'Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Sa'd [[In H, A: "Sa'id", and the text follows M and Tafsir al-Tabari.]] ibn Hisham, who said: I came to 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, and I said to her: "Inform me about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not recite: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?"
Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i have narrated something similar from the hadith of al-Hasan. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1352; Sunan An-Nasa'i (3/220).]]
Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, and Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abu az-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed the pilgrimage and entered upon 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, and I asked her about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "The character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
Thus Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. An-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Al-Musnad (6/188); Sunan An-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11138.]]
The meaning of this is that, peace be upon him, his following of the Qur'an, in its commands and prohibitions, became a natural disposition for him and a character he had made habitual, and he set aside his innate nature. Whatever the Qur'an commanded him, he did; whatever it forbade him, he abandoned. This was in addition to the tremendous character God had created in him: modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, forbearance, and every beautiful character trait. As is established in the Two Sahihs from Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for ten years, and he never said to me, "Uff," and never said to me about something I had done, "Why did you do it?" nor about something I had not done, "Why did you not do it?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in character. I never touched silk or brocade, nor anything softer than the palm of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and I never smelled musk or perfume more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6038; Sahih Muslim, no. 2309.]]
Al-Bukhari said: [Ahmad ibn Sa'id Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us] [[Addition from M, A, and Sahih al-Bukhari.]] Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in face and the best of people in form, neither excessively tall nor short. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3549.]]
The hadiths on this are many, and Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has a book on this subject, the "Shama'il."
Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor a woman, nor did he ever strike anything with his hand, except when fighting in the way of God. He was never given a choice between two things except that he chose the easier of them, so long as it was not sinful; and if it was sinful, he was the furthest of people from it. He never took revenge for himself for anything done to him, unless the sanctities of God were violated, in which case he took revenge for God, Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/232).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was only sent to perfect good character." He alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/381).]]

And His saying: ﴿So you will see and they will see, which of you is the afflicted.﴾ This means: so you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and deniers will know, who among you and them is the afflicted, the one who is misguided. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent.﴾ [Al-Qamar: 26], and like His saying: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ [Saba': 24].
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: the madness. Mujahid and others said likewise. Qatadah and others said: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: which of you is more in need of the devil.
The meaning of "the afflicted" is clear: the one who has been led astray from the truth and has strayed from it. The preposition "bi" entered into His saying ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ to indicate that the verb in His saying ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾ carries an implied sense, and its implied meaning is: "So you will know and they will know," or "So you will be informed and they will be informed of which of you is the afflicted." And God knows best.
Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided.﴾ This means: He, Exalted, knows which of the two groups, you or they, is the guided one, and He knows the party that has strayed from the truth.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Shabib al-Muktib narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ A tablet of light, and a pen of light, running with what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection." This is mursal and gharib.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that this pen is of light, its length being a hundred years.

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is an inkwell, and the ﴿Qalam﴾ is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatada regarding His saying ﴿Nun﴾, they both said: it is the inkwell.

A raised hadith of extreme strangeness has been narrated on this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created the Nun, which is the inkwell."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, my brother 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Thabit al-Thumali narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah created the Nun - which is the inkwell - and created the pen, and said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection of deed done, whether righteous or wicked, or provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful." Then He bound each thing of that, its affair: its entry into the world, how long its stay therein, and how its exit will be. Then He placed over the servants guardians, and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day from the keepers the deed of that day. When the provision is exhausted, the trace is cut off, and the term has ended, the guardians come to the keepers seeking the deed of that day. The keepers say to them: "We find nothing for your companion with us," so the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: So Ibn 'Abbas said: "Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29]? And is copying anything but from an original?"

* *

As for His saying ﴿By the pen﴾, the apparent meaning is that it is the genus of the pen with which one writes, as in His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾ [al-'Alaq: 3-5]. So it is an oath by Him, exalted be He, and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them by teaching writing, through which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada said: meaning: what they write.

Abu al-Duha said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, i.e., what they do.

al-Suddi said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, meaning the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants.

Others said: rather, what is meant here by the pen is the pen which Allah set running by the decree when He wrote the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They cited in this the hadiths reported concerning the mention of the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Yunus ibn Habib both said: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym al-Sulami narrated to us, from 'Ata' - that is Ibn Abi Rabah - Al-Walid ibn 'Ubada ibn al-Samit narrated to me, who said: My father called me when death came to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: "Write!" It said: "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree [what has been] and what will occur forever."'"

This hadith has been narrated by Imam Ahmad through several chains, from al-Walid ibn 'Ubada, from his father, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with it, and said: hasan sahih gharib. Abu Dawud narrated it in his book "al-Sunna" of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from Ibn Rabah, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla, from Abu Hafsa - whose name is Hubaysh ibn Shurayh al-Habashi al-Shami - from 'Ubada, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tusi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Rabah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, so He commanded it, and it wrote everything." Strange from this route, and they did not transmit it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿By the pen﴾, meaning: that with which the Reminder was written.

* *
His saying, ﴿and what they write﴾, means: what they write, as was mentioned earlier.

* *
His saying, ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾, means: you are not, praise be to God, a madman, as some ignorant people among your folk may say, those who deny the guidance and clear truth you have brought them, and so they attribute madness to you because of it. ﴿Indeed, for you there is a reward never cut off﴾ means: rather, for you there is a great reward and an abundant recompense that does not end and does not perish, for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and for your patience with their harm. The meaning of ﴿never cut off﴾ is: not interrupted, like His saying: ﴿a gift not withdrawn﴾ [Hud: 108], and ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾ [At-Tin: 6], meaning not cut off from them. Mujahid said: ﴿never cut off﴾ means: not counted, and this returns to what we have stated.

* *
His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means, indeed you are upon a tremendous religion [[In A: "upon a tremendous character".]], which is Islam. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said likewise.
'Atiyyah said: upon a tremendous courtesy (adab).
Ma'mar reported from Qatadah: 'A'ishah was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "His character was the Qur'an," meaning she would recite as it is in the Qur'an.
Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah reported from Qatadah concerning His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾: it was mentioned to us that Sa'd [[In A: "A, Sa'id".]] ibn Hisham asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa [[In A: "Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa".]], from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I asked 'A'ishah, and I said: "Inform me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/245).]]
This is a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in full in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah [[Sahih Muslim, no. 746.]], and it will come in Surah Al-Muzzammil, God willing.
Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Al-Hasan, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Al-Musnad (6/216).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Qays ibn Wahb, from a man of the Banu Sawad, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?" I said: "Tell me about that." She said: "I prepared food for him, and Hafsah prepared food for him. I said to my slave-girl: Go, and if she comes with the food and places it before him first, then throw the food down!" She said: "So she came with the food, and the slave-girl turned, and the dish fell and broke, and it was a leather mat [[In H, M, A: "nit'", and the text follows Al-Musnad.]]." She said: "So the Messenger of God gathered it up and said: 'Give it [or: give it, O such-and-such] a dish in place of your dish.'" [Aswad was unsure whether it was "give" in the masculine or feminine form.] She said: "And he said nothing."
Ibn Jarir said: 'Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Sa'd [[In H, A: "Sa'id", and the text follows M and Tafsir al-Tabari.]] ibn Hisham, who said: I came to 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, and I said to her: "Inform me about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not recite: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?"
Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i have narrated something similar from the hadith of al-Hasan. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1352; Sunan An-Nasa'i (3/220).]]
Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, and Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abu az-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed the pilgrimage and entered upon 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, and I asked her about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "The character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
Thus Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. An-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Al-Musnad (6/188); Sunan An-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11138.]]
The meaning of this is that, peace be upon him, his following of the Qur'an, in its commands and prohibitions, became a natural disposition for him and a character he had made habitual, and he set aside his innate nature. Whatever the Qur'an commanded him, he did; whatever it forbade him, he abandoned. This was in addition to the tremendous character God had created in him: modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, forbearance, and every beautiful character trait. As is established in the Two Sahihs from Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for ten years, and he never said to me, "Uff," and never said to me about something I had done, "Why did you do it?" nor about something I had not done, "Why did you not do it?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in character. I never touched silk or brocade, nor anything softer than the palm of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and I never smelled musk or perfume more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6038; Sahih Muslim, no. 2309.]]
Al-Bukhari said: [Ahmad ibn Sa'id Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us] [[Addition from M, A, and Sahih al-Bukhari.]] Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in face and the best of people in form, neither excessively tall nor short. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3549.]]
The hadiths on this are many, and Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has a book on this subject, the "Shama'il."
Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor a woman, nor did he ever strike anything with his hand, except when fighting in the way of God. He was never given a choice between two things except that he chose the easier of them, so long as it was not sinful; and if it was sinful, he was the furthest of people from it. He never took revenge for himself for anything done to him, unless the sanctities of God were violated, in which case he took revenge for God, Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/232).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was only sent to perfect good character." He alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/381).]]

And His saying: ﴿So you will see and they will see, which of you is the afflicted.﴾ This means: so you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and deniers will know, who among you and them is the afflicted, the one who is misguided. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent.﴾ [Al-Qamar: 26], and like His saying: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ [Saba': 24].
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: the madness. Mujahid and others said likewise. Qatadah and others said: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: which of you is more in need of the devil.
The meaning of "the afflicted" is clear: the one who has been led astray from the truth and has strayed from it. The preposition "bi" entered into His saying ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ to indicate that the verb in His saying ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾ carries an implied sense, and its implied meaning is: "So you will know and they will know," or "So you will be informed and they will be informed of which of you is the afflicted." And God knows best.
Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided.﴾ This means: He, Exalted, knows which of the two groups, you or they, is the guided one, and He knows the party that has strayed from the truth.

Commentary of Tafsir of Surah al-Qalam (Surah 68)

It is a Meccan surah. (Note: the source text states it is Madani; translating as given.)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hija') has already passed at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and that ﴿Nun﴾ is like ﴿Sad﴾ and ﴿Qaf﴾ and similar disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs. The matter has been examined there sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a great fish upon the surging of the vast encompassing water, and it is the bearer of the seven earths, as the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan - that is al-Thawri - narrated to us, Sulayman - that is al-A'mash - narrated to us, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree." So it ran with what would happen from that day until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" and raised the vapour of the water, and from it the sky was split open, and the earth was spread out on the back of the Nun. The Nun then convulsed, and the earth shook, so it was made firm with the mountains, for indeed they boast over the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it similarly from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Likewise it was narrated by Shu'ba, Muhammad ibn Fudayl, and Waki', from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Shu'ba added in his narration: Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Sharik narrated it from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan - or Mujahid - from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar. Ma'mar narrated from al-A'mash that Ibn 'Abbas said... and mentioned it, then recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed the first thing my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, created was the pen. Then He said to it: "Write!" So it wrote what is to occur until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" above the water, then He pressed the earth upon it.

Al-Tabarani has narrated this raised (marfu') as well. He said: Abu Habib - Zayd ibn al-Muhtadi al-Marwazi - narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Taliqani narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the first things Allah created were the pen and the fish. He said to the pen: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Every existing thing until the Day of Resurrection.'" Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ So the "Nun" is the fish, and the "Qalam" is the pen.

Another narration on this: Ibn 'Asakir narrated it from Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He created the 'Nun', which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur - or: what is existing - of deed, or provision, or trace, or term.' So it wrote that until the Day of Resurrection, and that is His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Then He sealed the pen, and it has not spoken until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: 'By My might, I shall perfect you in whomever I love, and I shall diminish you in whomever I hate.'"

Ibn Abi Najih said: Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed him, from Mujahid, who said: It was said: "The Nun is the great fish beneath the seventh earth."

Al-Baghawi and a group of the exegetes mentioned: that upon the back of this fish is a rock whose thickness is like the thickness of the heavens and the earth, and upon its back is a bull having forty thousand horns, and upon its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them. Allah knows best. And it is strange that some of them applied this meaning to the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Isma'il narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas: that 'Abd Allah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madina, so he came to him and asked him about things. He said: "I will ask you about things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise eat? Why does the child resemble its father, and why does the child resemble its mother?" He said: "Jibril informed me of them just now." Ibn Salam said: "He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." He said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise eat, it is the caudate lobe of the fish's liver. As for the child, when the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child resembles the man, and when the woman's water precedes the man's water, she resembles her."

Al-Bukhari narrated it through several chains from Humayd, and Muslim also narrated it. And in it, from the hadith of Thawban, mawla of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), something similar. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Thawban: that a rabbi asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about questions, and among them he said: "What is their gift?" - meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise - He said: "The caudate lobe of the fish's liver." He said: "What is their nourishment after it?" He said: "The bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which used to graze on its edges." He said: "What is their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring therein called Salsabil."

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a tablet of light.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Shabib al-Muktib narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ A tablet of light, and a pen of light, running with what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection." This is mursal and gharib.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that this pen is of light, its length being a hundred years.

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is an inkwell, and the ﴿Qalam﴾ is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatada regarding His saying ﴿Nun﴾, they both said: it is the inkwell.

A raised hadith of extreme strangeness has been narrated on this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created the Nun, which is the inkwell."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, my brother 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Thabit al-Thumali narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah created the Nun - which is the inkwell - and created the pen, and said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection of deed done, whether righteous or wicked, or provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful." Then He bound each thing of that, its affair: its entry into the world, how long its stay therein, and how its exit will be. Then He placed over the servants guardians, and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day from the keepers the deed of that day. When the provision is exhausted, the trace is cut off, and the term has ended, the guardians come to the keepers seeking the deed of that day. The keepers say to them: "We find nothing for your companion with us," so the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: So Ibn 'Abbas said: "Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29]? And is copying anything but from an original?"

* *

As for His saying ﴿By the pen﴾, the apparent meaning is that it is the genus of the pen with which one writes, as in His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾ [al-'Alaq: 3-5]. So it is an oath by Him, exalted be He, and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them by teaching writing, through which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada said: meaning: what they write.

Abu al-Duha said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, i.e., what they do.

al-Suddi said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, meaning the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants.

Others said: rather, what is meant here by the pen is the pen which Allah set running by the decree when He wrote the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They cited in this the hadiths reported concerning the mention of the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Yunus ibn Habib both said: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym al-Sulami narrated to us, from 'Ata' - that is Ibn Abi Rabah - Al-Walid ibn 'Ubada ibn al-Samit narrated to me, who said: My father called me when death came to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: "Write!" It said: "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree [what has been] and what will occur forever."'"

This hadith has been narrated by Imam Ahmad through several chains, from al-Walid ibn 'Ubada, from his father, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with it, and said: hasan sahih gharib. Abu Dawud narrated it in his book "al-Sunna" of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from Ibn Rabah, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla, from Abu Hafsa - whose name is Hubaysh ibn Shurayh al-Habashi al-Shami - from 'Ubada, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tusi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Rabah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, so He commanded it, and it wrote everything." Strange from this route, and they did not transmit it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿By the pen﴾, meaning: that with which the Reminder was written.

* *
His saying, ﴿and what they write﴾, means: what they write, as was mentioned earlier.

* *
His saying, ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾, means: you are not, praise be to God, a madman, as some ignorant people among your folk may say, those who deny the guidance and clear truth you have brought them, and so they attribute madness to you because of it. ﴿Indeed, for you there is a reward never cut off﴾ means: rather, for you there is a great reward and an abundant recompense that does not end and does not perish, for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and for your patience with their harm. The meaning of ﴿never cut off﴾ is: not interrupted, like His saying: ﴿a gift not withdrawn﴾ [Hud: 108], and ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾ [At-Tin: 6], meaning not cut off from them. Mujahid said: ﴿never cut off﴾ means: not counted, and this returns to what we have stated.

* *
His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means, indeed you are upon a tremendous religion [[In A: "upon a tremendous character".]], which is Islam. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said likewise.
'Atiyyah said: upon a tremendous courtesy (adab).
Ma'mar reported from Qatadah: 'A'ishah was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "His character was the Qur'an," meaning she would recite as it is in the Qur'an.
Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah reported from Qatadah concerning His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾: it was mentioned to us that Sa'd [[In A: "A, Sa'id".]] ibn Hisham asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa [[In A: "Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa".]], from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I asked 'A'ishah, and I said: "Inform me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/245).]]
This is a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in full in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah [[Sahih Muslim, no. 746.]], and it will come in Surah Al-Muzzammil, God willing.
Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Al-Hasan, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Al-Musnad (6/216).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Qays ibn Wahb, from a man of the Banu Sawad, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?" I said: "Tell me about that." She said: "I prepared food for him, and Hafsah prepared food for him. I said to my slave-girl: Go, and if she comes with the food and places it before him first, then throw the food down!" She said: "So she came with the food, and the slave-girl turned, and the dish fell and broke, and it was a leather mat [[In H, M, A: "nit'", and the text follows Al-Musnad.]]." She said: "So the Messenger of God gathered it up and said: 'Give it [or: give it, O such-and-such] a dish in place of your dish.'" [Aswad was unsure whether it was "give" in the masculine or feminine form.] She said: "And he said nothing."
Ibn Jarir said: 'Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Sa'd [[In H, A: "Sa'id", and the text follows M and Tafsir al-Tabari.]] ibn Hisham, who said: I came to 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, and I said to her: "Inform me about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ)." She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not recite: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?"
Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i have narrated something similar from the hadith of al-Hasan. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1352; Sunan An-Nasa'i (3/220).]]
Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, and Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abu az-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed the pilgrimage and entered upon 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, and I asked her about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "The character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."
Thus Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. An-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Al-Musnad (6/188); Sunan An-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11138.]]
The meaning of this is that, peace be upon him, his following of the Qur'an, in its commands and prohibitions, became a natural disposition for him and a character he had made habitual, and he set aside his innate nature. Whatever the Qur'an commanded him, he did; whatever it forbade him, he abandoned. This was in addition to the tremendous character God had created in him: modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, forbearance, and every beautiful character trait. As is established in the Two Sahihs from Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for ten years, and he never said to me, "Uff," and never said to me about something I had done, "Why did you do it?" nor about something I had not done, "Why did you not do it?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in character. I never touched silk or brocade, nor anything softer than the palm of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and I never smelled musk or perfume more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6038; Sahih Muslim, no. 2309.]]
Al-Bukhari said: [Ahmad ibn Sa'id Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us] [[Addition from M, A, and Sahih al-Bukhari.]] Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the best of people in face and the best of people in form, neither excessively tall nor short. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3549.]]
The hadiths on this are many, and Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has a book on this subject, the "Shama'il."
Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor a woman, nor did he ever strike anything with his hand, except when fighting in the way of God. He was never given a choice between two things except that he chose the easier of them, so long as it was not sinful; and if it was sinful, he was the furthest of people from it. He never took revenge for himself for anything done to him, unless the sanctities of God were violated, in which case he took revenge for God, Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/232).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was only sent to perfect good character." He alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/381).]]

And His saying: ﴿So you will see and they will see, which of you is the afflicted.﴾ This means: so you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and deniers will know, who among you and them is the afflicted, the one who is misguided. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent.﴾ [Al-Qamar: 26], and like His saying: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ [Saba': 24].
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: "You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection."
Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: the madness. Mujahid and others said likewise. Qatadah and others said: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ means: which of you is more in need of the devil.
The meaning of "the afflicted" is clear: the one who has been led astray from the truth and has strayed from it. The preposition "bi" entered into His saying ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾ to indicate that the verb in His saying ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾ carries an implied sense, and its implied meaning is: "So you will know and they will know," or "So you will be informed and they will be informed of which of you is the afflicted." And God knows best.
Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided.﴾ This means: He, Exalted, knows which of the two groups, you or they, is the guided one, and He knows the party that has strayed from the truth.

Commentary of Tafsir of Surah al-Qalam (Surah 68)

It is a Meccan surah. (Note: the source text states it is Madani; translating as given.)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hija') has already passed at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and that ﴿Nun﴾ is like ﴿Sad﴾ and ﴿Qaf﴾ and similar disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs. The matter has been examined there sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

It has also been said that what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a great fish upon the surging of the vast encompassing water, and it is the bearer of the seven earths, as the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Sufyan - that is al-Thawri - narrated to us, Sulayman - that is al-A'mash - narrated to us, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree." So it ran with what would happen from that day until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" and raised the vapour of the water, and from it the sky was split open, and the earth was spread out on the back of the Nun. The Nun then convulsed, and the earth shook, so it was made firm with the mountains, for indeed they boast over the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it similarly from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Likewise it was narrated by Shu'ba, Muhammad ibn Fudayl, and Waki', from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Shu'ba added in his narration: Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Sharik narrated it from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan - or Mujahid - from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar. Ma'mar narrated from al-A'mash that Ibn 'Abbas said... and mentioned it, then recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed the first thing my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, created was the pen. Then He said to it: "Write!" So it wrote what is to occur until the Hour arises. Then He created the "Nun" above the water, then He pressed the earth upon it.

Al-Tabarani has narrated this raised (marfu') as well. He said: Abu Habib - Zayd ibn al-Muhtadi al-Marwazi - narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Taliqani narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the first things Allah created were the pen and the fish. He said to the pen: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Every existing thing until the Day of Resurrection.'" Then he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ So the "Nun" is the fish, and the "Qalam" is the pen.

Another narration on this: Ibn 'Asakir narrated it from Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He created the 'Nun', which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: 'Write!' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur - or: what is existing - of deed, or provision, or trace, or term.' So it wrote that until the Day of Resurrection, and that is His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ Then He sealed the pen, and it has not spoken until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: 'By My might, I shall perfect you in whomever I love, and I shall diminish you in whomever I hate.'"

Ibn Abi Najih said: Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed him, from Mujahid, who said: It was said: "The Nun is the great fish beneath the seventh earth."

Al-Baghawi and a group of the exegetes mentioned: that upon the back of this fish is a rock whose thickness is like the thickness of the heavens and the earth, and upon its back is a bull having forty thousand horns, and upon its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them. Allah knows best. And it is strange that some of them applied this meaning to the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Isma'il narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas: that 'Abd Allah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madina, so he came to him and asked him about things. He said: "I will ask you about things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise eat? Why does the child resemble its father, and why does the child resemble its mother?" He said: "Jibril informed me of them just now." Ibn Salam said: "He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." He said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise eat, it is the caudate lobe of the fish's liver. As for the child, when the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child resembles the man, and when the woman's water precedes the man's water, she resembles her."

Al-Bukhari narrated it through several chains from Humayd, and Muslim also narrated it. And in it, from the hadith of Thawban, mawla of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), something similar. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Thawban: that a rabbi asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about questions, and among them he said: "What is their gift?" - meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise - He said: "The caudate lobe of the fish's liver." He said: "What is their nourishment after it?" He said: "The bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which used to graze on its edges." He said: "What is their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring therein called Salsabil."

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is a tablet of light.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Shabib al-Muktib narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.﴾ A tablet of light, and a pen of light, running with what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection." This is mursal and gharib.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that this pen is of light, its length being a hundred years.

It has also been said: what is meant by ﴿Nun﴾ is an inkwell, and the ﴿Qalam﴾ is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatada regarding His saying ﴿Nun﴾, they both said: it is the inkwell.

A raised hadith of extreme strangeness has been narrated on this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Abd Allah, mawla of the Banu Umayya, narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created the Nun, which is the inkwell."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, my brother 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Thabit al-Thumali narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah created the Nun - which is the inkwell - and created the pen, and said: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection of deed done, whether righteous or wicked, or provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful." Then He bound each thing of that, its affair: its entry into the world, how long its stay therein, and how its exit will be. Then He placed over the servants guardians, and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day from the keepers the deed of that day. When the provision is exhausted, the trace is cut off, and the term has ended, the guardians come to the keepers seeking the deed of that day. The keepers say to them: "We find nothing for your companion with us," so the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: So Ibn 'Abbas said: "Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29]? And is copying anything but from an original?"

* *

As for His saying ﴿By the pen﴾, the apparent meaning is that it is the genus of the pen with which one writes, as in His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾ [al-'Alaq: 3-5]. So it is an oath by Him, exalted be He, and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them by teaching writing, through which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada said: meaning: what they write.

Abu al-Duha said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, i.e., what they do.

al-Suddi said: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾, meaning the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants.

Others said: rather, what is meant here by the pen is the pen which Allah set running by the decree when He wrote the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They cited in this the hadiths reported concerning the mention of the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Yunus ibn Habib both said: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym al-Sulami narrated to us, from 'Ata' - that is Ibn Abi Rabah - Al-Walid ibn 'Ubada ibn al-Samit narrated to me, who said: My father called me when death came to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: "Write!" It said: "O Lord, what shall I write?" He said: "Write the decree [what has been] and what will occur forever."'"

This hadith has been narrated by Imam Ahmad through several chains, from al-Walid ibn 'Ubada, from his father, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with it, and said: hasan sahih gharib. Abu Dawud narrated it in his book "al-Sunna" of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from Ibn Rabah, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla, from Abu Hafsa - whose name is Hubaysh ibn Shurayh al-Habashi al-Shami - from 'Ubada, and mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tusi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Rabah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, so He commanded it, and it wrote everything." Strange from this route, and they did not transmit it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿By the pen﴾, meaning: that with which the Reminder was written.

* *
His saying, ﴿and what they write﴾, means: what they write, as was mentioned earlier.

* *
His saying, ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾, means: you are not, praise be to God, a madman, as some ignorant people among your folk may say, those who deny the guidance and clear truth you have brought them, and so they attribute madness to you because of it. ﴿Indeed, for you there is a reward never cut off﴾ means: rather, for you there is a great reward and an abundant recompense that does not end and does not perish, for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and for your patience with their harm. The meaning of ﴿never cut off﴾ is: not interrupted, like His saying: ﴿a gift not withdrawn﴾ [Hud: 108], and ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾ [At-Tin: 6], meaning not cut off from them. Mujahid said: ﴿never cut off﴾ means: not counted, and this returns to what we have stated.

* *
His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means, indeed you are upon a tremendous religion [[In A: "upon a tremendous character".]], which is Islam. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said likewise.
'Atiyyah said: upon a tremendous courtesy (adab).
Ma'mar reported from Qatadah: 'A'ishah was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "His character was the Qur'an," meaning she would recite as it is in the Qur'an.
Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah reported from Qatadah concerning His saying, ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾: it was mentioned to us that Sa'd [[In A: "A, Sa'id".]] ibn Hisham asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an."

She said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/245).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Al-Hasan, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Al-Musnad (6/216).]]
Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Qays ibn Wahb, from a man of the Banu Sawad, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?" I said: "Tell me about that." She said: "I prepared food for him, and Hafsah prepared food for him. I said to my slave-girl: Go, and if she comes with the food and places it before him first, then throw the food down!" She said: "So she came with the food, and the slave-girl turned, and the dish fell and broke, and it was a leather mat [[In H, M, A: "nit'", and the text follows Al-Musnad.]]." [Aswad was unsure whether it was "give" in the masculine or feminine form.] She said: "And he said nothing."

She said: "His character was the Qur'an. Do you not recite: ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾?"

Thus Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. An-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/13); Al-Musnad (6/188); Sunan An-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11138.]]
