[[Al-Musnad (4/227). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/393): "Its chain is good (isnad hasan), except that Ibn Ghanm did not hear from the Prophet (ﷺ)." And he said elsewhere (7/128): "In it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, whom a group declared trustworthy, but there is weakness in him, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm has no companionship (sahabah) according to the correct view."]]

With this same chain, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The jawwaz, the ja'zari, the 'utull, the zanim will not enter Paradise." [[Al-Musnad (4/227).]] Some of the Successors (tabi'un) also narrated it as a mursal (a report where the Companion is omitted from the chain).

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sky weeps over a servant whom Allah has made healthy in body, broad in belly, and given a small share of the world, yet he is a wrongdoer toward people." He said: "That is the 'utull zanim." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/16). It is a mursal report.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated the same in two mursal routes, and a number of the early generations (al-salaf) stated it explicitly, among them Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others: that the 'utull is the one of strong build, powerful in eating, drinking, sexual intercourse, and other matters.

As for the zanim, al-Bukhari said: Mahmud narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Coarse, after that, base-born﴾: "A man of Quraysh who had a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep."

The meaning of this is that he was notorious for evil, like the notoriety of the sheep that has a zanamah (wattle) among its counterparts. In the language of the Arabs, al-zanim is the illegitimate claimant among a people (al-da'i fi al-qawm). This was said by Ibn Jarir and a number of the imams. He said: From this is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit, meaning disparaging some of the disbelievers of Quraysh:

"And you are a zanim, attached among the family of Hashim, as the single cup is attached behind the rider."

And another said:

"A zanim whose father is not known, the son of a promiscuous mother, of base lineage..."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ammar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, from Hisham, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿zanim﴾: "The da'i (illegitimate claimant), the vile, the base." Then Ibn 'Abbas said:

"A zanim, whom men claim as an addition, as the shins are added to the hide's edge."

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The zanim is the da'i." It is also said: "The zanim is a man who had a zanamah by which he was recognized." It is also said: "He is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, ally of Banu Zuhrah." Some people of Banu Zuhrah claimed that the zanim was al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth al-Zuhri, but this is not so.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he claimed the zanim is "the one attached in lineage (al-mulhaq al-nasab)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he heard him say regarding this verse, ﴿Coarse, after that, base-born﴾: Sa'id said: "He is the one attached to a people, who is not one of them."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amir ibn Qudamah, who said: 'Ikrimah was asked about the zanim, and he said: "He is the illegitimate child (walad al-zina)."

al-Hakam ibn Aban said, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿Coarse, after that, base-born﴾: "The believer is distinguished from the disbeliever like the zanmaa sheep." The zanmaa among sheep is the one that has two dangling pieces hanging from its throat.

al-Thawri said, from Jabir, from al-Hasan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The zanim is the one known for evil as the sheep is known by its zanamah. The zanim is the attached one." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

He also narrated through the route of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding the zanim: "He was described but not recognized until it was said: zanim. He had a zanamah on his neck by which he was known." Others said: "He was a da'i."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from the people of tafsir (ashab al-tafsir), who said: "He is the one who has a zanamah like the zanamah of a sheep."

al-Dahhak said: "He had a zanamah at the base of his ear." It is also said: "He is the base one, attached in lineage."

Abu Ishaq said, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "He is the suspicious one, known for evil."

Mujahid said: "The zanim is one known by this description as the sheep is known." Abu Razin said: "The zanim is a sign of disbelief." 'Ikrimah said: "The zanim is one known for baseness as the sheep is known by its zanamah."

Among the views on this are many, and they all come back to what we have said: that the zanim is the one well known for evil, recognized as such among people, and he is usually an illegitimate claimant of lineage (da'i) who is also a product of fornication (zina). For generally Satan dominates him more than he dominates others. As has come in the hadith: "The child of fornication will not enter Paradise" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/203) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him, and narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra under numbers (4925, 4926) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it among the fabricated reports (al-Mawdu'at) (3/111) and said: "It contradicts the principles, and the greatest of these is the saying of the Exalted: 'No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another' (35:18)." Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, responding to Ibn al-Jawzi in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 133), said: "It does not conflict with that if it is authentic, for He did not bar him from Paradise because of his parents' deeds, but because a corrupt drop of semen does not in general produce something good, and only a good soul enters Paradise. So if within this kind there is a good one, he enters Paradise, and the hadith is one of the general statements that is restricted. It has also been reported in a narration: 'He is the worst of the three,' and it is a good hadith, and its meaning is sound in this respect, for the worst of the two parents is an accident, whereas this is a corrupt drop, so his evil is in his origin, and the evil of the parents is in their actions."] I say: it may also be explained by the qualification in the hadith of 'A'ishah cited below, that he is the worst of the three when he acts according to the deeds of his parents. Ibn al-Jawzi's criticism applies to the hadith: "The child of fornication will be in the Fire down to seven generations," and it is fabricated.[[Its wording is as stated.]] In another hadith: "The child of fornication is the worst of the three when he acts according to the deeds of his two parents" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad (6/109) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and (2/311) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿Because he has wealth and sons. When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ The Exalted says: This is in exchange for what Allah bestowed upon him of wealth and sons; he disbelieved in the signs of Allah and turned away from them, and claimed that they were falsehood taken from the tales of the ancients. Like His saying: ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone, and to whom I gave vast wealth, and sons present with him, and smoothed for him [his path] with smoothing. Then he desires that I should add more. No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our signs. I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent. Indeed, he thought and deliberated, so may he be destroyed, how he deliberated. Then may he be destroyed, how he deliberated. Then he considered. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned back and was arrogant. And he said, "This is not but magic transmitted. This is not but the word of a human."﴾ Allah said: ﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11–26]. Here the Exalted said: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout.﴾
Ibn Jarir said: We will make his matter clear, so that they recognize him and it is not hidden from them, just as a brand is not hidden on snouts. Qatadah likewise said: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾: a disgrace that never leaves him, the last thing that remains on him.
In another report from him: a mark upon his nose. Al-Suddi also said so.
Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾: he will fight on the day of Badr, and will be struck on the nose with the sword in battle. Others said: ﴿We will brand him﴾ with the mark of the people of the Fire, meaning we will blacken his face on the Day of Resurrection, and he expressed the face by the snout. Ibn Jarir related all of this and inclined to the view that there is no obstacle to all of it being combined, both in this world and the Hereafter, and this is a sound position.
Ibn Abi Hatim, in the commentary on Surah ﴿Concerning what are they asking one another?﴾, said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih the scribe of al-Layth narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, Khalid narrated to me from Sa'id, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abdullah, from Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed a servant is recorded as a believer for ages upon ages, then he dies while Allah is displeased with him. And indeed a servant is recorded as a disbeliever for ages upon ages, then he dies while Allah is pleased with him. Whoever dies as a backbiter and slanderer, deriding people, his sign on the Day of Resurrection is that Allah brands him on the snout, on both lips." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (60) "the lost fragment" and al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (3234) "Majma' al-Bahrayn" from al-Mutalib al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Salih with the same chain. He said in al-Awsat: "It is not narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr except with this chain; al-Layth alone transmitted it."]].

This is a parable which Allah, the Exalted, struck for the disbelievers of Quraysh concerning the great mercy He sent to them and the abundant blessings He bestowed upon them, namely His sending Muhammad (ﷺ) to them. They met him with denial, rejection and warfare. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, We have tested them﴾, i.e., We tried them, ﴿as We tested the companions of the garden﴾, which was an orchard containing various kinds of fruits and produce, ﴿when they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾, i.e., they swore among themselves that they would cut its fruit by night, so that no poor man or beggar would notice them, so that its produce would be entirely theirs and they would give nothing of it in charity. ﴿And they did not make an exception﴾, i.e., in what they swore. Therefore Allah nullified their oaths, saying: ﴿Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep﴾, i.e., a calamity from heaven struck it, ﴿so it became like the black night﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., like the pitch-black night. Al-Thawri and al-Suddi said: like a field of crops after it has been harvested, i.e., dry, withered stubble.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ahmad ibn al-Sabbah: Bishr ibn Zadhan informed us, from 'Umar ibn Subh [[In manuscript A: "ibn Subayh".]], from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of sins. Indeed, a servant may commit a sin and thereby be deprived of a provision that had been prepared for him." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep, so it became like the black night﴾. They were deprived of the best of their garden because of their sin. [[In the chain of 'Umar ibn Subh, Ibn Hibban said: he was among those who fabricated hadith. Al-Daraqutni said: abandoned (matruk). Al-Azdi said: a liar. The hadith has a supporting report from the hadith of Thawban, may Allah be pleased with him, which Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad (5/277).]]

﴿Then they called out to one another in the morning﴾, i.e., when the morning came, some of them called to others to go out to the harvesting. ﴿Go out early to your field if you intend to harvest﴾, i.e., if you wish to cut the fruit. Mujahid said: their field was grapes.

﴿So they set out, whispering to one another﴾, i.e., conferring secretly among themselves so that no one would hear their words. Then Allah, the Knower of the secret and what is concealed, explained what they were whispering, saying: ﴿So they set out, whispering, [saying], "No poor man shall enter it today upon you."﴾ i.e., some of them said to others: "Do not let any poor person enter it today against you!"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they went early, determined﴾, i.e., with power and vehemence. Mujahid said: ﴿determined﴾ means with diligence. 'Ikrimah said: with anger. Al-Sha'bi said: ﴿determined﴾ means against the poor. Al-Suddi said: ﴿determined﴾, i.e., the name of their village was Harad. Al-Suddi went too far in this view!

﴿Capable﴾, i.e., capable of it, according to what they claimed and presumed.

﴿But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we have gone astray."﴾ i.e., when they reached it and looked upon it, and it was in the state Allah described, having transformed from that freshness, brightness and abundance of fruit into something black and utterly dark, from which nothing could be benefited, they believed they had taken the wrong road. Therefore they said: ﴿Indeed, we have gone astray﴾, i.e., we have taken a road other than the right one and lost our way to it. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. Then they returned from what they had been in and became certain that it was indeed their garden, so they said: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾, i.e., rather, this is it, but we have no share and no portion in it.

﴿The best of them said﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: i.e., the most just of them and the best of them. ﴿Did I not tell you, "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?"﴾ Mujahid, al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Why do you not glorify [Allah]?﴾ means: why do you not make an exception [in your oath]? Al-Suddi said: their making an exception at that time was glorification.

Ibn Jurayj said: it is the saying of the one who says: "If Allah wills." It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿The best of them said: "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify [Allah]?'"﴾ i.e., why do you not glorify Allah and thank Him for what He has given you and bestowed upon you? ﴿They said: "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾ They performed obedience at a time when it would not benefit them, and they regretted and confessed at a time when it would not avail. Therefore they said: ﴿Indeed, we were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Then some of them turned upon others, blaming one another﴾, i.e., some blamed others for having persisted in preventing the poor from their due in the harvest. So the answer of each to the other was nothing but admission of sin and guilt. ﴿They said: "Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors."﴾ i.e., we aggressed, rebelled, exceeded and went beyond the limit, until what has befallen us befell us. ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning to our Lord [in hope].﴾ It was said: they desired that He would grant them its replacement in this world. It was also said: they sought its reward in the Hereafter. And Allah knows best.

Then some of the early scholars (salaf) mentioned that these people were from Yemen. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they were from a village called Darawan [[In manuscript A: "Jirdan".]], six miles from San'a'. It was also said: they were from Abyssinia. Their father had left them this garden, and they were people of the Book. Their father used to manage it in a good manner: he would spend from its produce on its upkeep, store for his family the food of their year, and give the surplus in charity. When he died, his sons inherited it and said: "Our father was foolish, for he used to set aside some of this for the poor. If we withheld it from them, it would all be ours in abundance." When they resolved upon that, they were punished with the opposite of their intention: Allah removed entirely what was in their hands, both the capital and the profit, and the charity, so nothing remained for them.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Such is the punishment﴾, i.e., thus is the punishment of one who opposes the command of Allah, withholds what Allah has given him and bestowed upon him, denies the right of the needy, the poor and those in want, and exchanges the blessing of Allah for disbelief. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ i.e., this is the punishment of this world as you have heard, but the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. It has been reported in a hadith narrated by the Hafiz al-Bayhaqi by way of Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade harvesting by night and reaping by night [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (4/133). He forbade it only for the sake of the poor, so that they might be present in the daytime and be given charity from it."]].

Therefore they said: ﴿Indeed, we were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Then some of them turned upon others, blaming one another﴾, i.e., some blamed others for having persisted in preventing the poor from their due in the harvest. So the answer of each to the other was nothing but admission of sin and guilt. ﴿They said: "Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors."﴾ i.e., we aggressed, rebelled, exceeded and went beyond the limit, until what has befallen us befell us. ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning to our Lord [in hope].﴾ It was said: they desired that He would grant them its replacement in this world. It was also said: they sought its reward in the Hereafter. And Allah knows best.

Then some of the early scholars (salaf) mentioned that these people were from Yemen. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they were from a village called Darawan [[In manuscript A: "Jirdan".]], six miles from San'a'. It was also said: they were from Abyssinia. Their father had left them this garden, and they were people of the Book. Their father used to manage it in a good manner: he would spend from its produce on its upkeep, store for his family the food of their year, and give the surplus in charity. When he died, his sons inherited it and said: "Our father was foolish, for he used to set aside some of this for the poor. If we withheld it from them, it would all be ours in abundance." When they resolved upon that, they were punished with the opposite of their intention: Allah removed entirely what was in their hands, both the capital and the profit, and the charity, so nothing remained for them.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Such is the punishment﴾, i.e., thus is the punishment of one who opposes the command of Allah, withholds what Allah has given him and bestowed upon him, denies the right of the needy, the poor and those in want, and exchanges the blessing of Allah for disbelief. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ i.e., this is the punishment of this world as you have heard, but the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. It has been reported in a hadith narrated by the Hafiz al-Bayhaqi by way of Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade harvesting by night and reaping by night [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (4/133). Al-jidad (with a fatha or kasra on the dal) — Ibn al-Athir said in al-Nihayah (1/244): "It is the cutting of palm dates, which is cutting their fruit; one says: jadda al-thamarah yajiduha jaddan. He forbade it only for the sake of the poor, so that they might be present in the daytime and be given charity from it."]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 68, verses 34–41:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the state of the people of the worldly garden and the punishment that befell them when they disobeyed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and opposed His command, He made clear that for those who fear Him and obey Him in the Hereafter there are the Gardens of Bliss, which do not perish, do not run out, and whose bliss never ends.

Then He said: ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ That is: Shall We equate these with those in reward? ﴿No! By your Lord, the Lord of the earth and the heaven!﴾ Therefore He said: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ That is: How do you think such a thing?

Then He said: ﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study, that you will surely have therein whatever you choose?﴾ He says: Do you have in your possession a Book sent down from the heaven that you study and memorize and transmit, the later generation from the earlier, containing a firm ruling as you claim? ﴿That you will surely have therein whatever you choose. Or do you have oaths from Us, binding until the Day of Resurrection, that you will surely have whatever you judge?﴾ That is: Do you have with you covenants from Us and firm pledges? ﴿That you will surely have whatever you judge﴾ That is: that you will certainly obtain what you desire and wish for. ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that.﴾ That is: Say to them: Who is it that guarantees and takes responsibility for this?

﴿Or do they have associates?﴾ That is: from among the idols and rivals. ﴿Then let them bring their associates, if they are truthful.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 68, verses 42–47:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) with Him [[In M: "with their Lord".]] are Gardens of Bliss, He explained when that will take place and occur, saying: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, and they will be summoned to prostrate, but they will not be able to﴾. He means: the Day of Resurrection, and what will occur in it of terrors, convulsions, trials, tests, and great matters. Al-Bukhari said here:

Adam narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. There will remain those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation, and they will go to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid plate." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4919).]]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs and in other works through various chains, with different wordings. It is a long, well-known hadith. [[It is the hadith of intercession, and its full text and wording were mentioned earlier in the tafsir of the first surah of al-Isra'.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Usamah ibn Zayd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "It is a day of distress and severity." Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud (or Ibn 'Abbas; the doubt is from Ibn Jarir) regarding: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "About a great matter," like the saying of the poet:

"And war stood up among us upon its shin."  [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (29/24).]]

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "The severity of the matter."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the first hour that will occur on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujahid: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "The severity of the matter and its seriousness."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas his statement: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that it is "the severe and dreadful matter of terror on the Day of Resurrection."

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas his statement: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "When the matter is uncovered and deeds are displayed. Its uncovering is entry into the Hereafter, and the uncovering of the matter from it." Likewise al-Dahhak and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir cited all of this, then said:

Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me: Harun ibn 'Umar al-Makhzumi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abu Sa'id Rawh ibn Janah narrated to us, from a client of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said regarding ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾: "From a great light, they will fall down prostrating to Him."

Abu Ya'la also narrated it, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/27) and Musnad Abi Ya'la (13/269).

Note: Some people thought that Ibn Kathir took here the path of ta'wil (figurative interpretation) regarding the attribute of the shin, and this is a mistaken understanding. This is because Ibn Kathir explained this verse by the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, then mentioned what was said about this verse. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim spoke about this verse with an excellent discussion. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah (1/252, 253): "The Companions differed in the interpretation of this verse: is the meaning the uncovering of severity, or is the meaning that the Lord, exalted is He, uncovers His shin? Nothing is reported from the Companions and Successors as a dispute about whether it is among the attributes or not, outside this context. Nothing in the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that this is an attribute of Allah, because He, glorified is He, did not attribute the shin to Himself, but mentioned it bare, without attribution and indefinite. Those who affirmed that it is an attribute, like the two hands and the finger, did not take that from the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, but affirmed it by the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, which is agreed upon as sound, the long hadith of intercession, in which is: 'Then the Lord will uncover His shin, and they will fall down prostrating to Him.' Whoever interprets the verse as that says: the statement of the Exalted, 'On the Day when the shin will be laid bare and they will be summoned to prostrate' (al-Qalam: 42), corresponds to the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Then He will uncover His shin, and they will fall down prostrating to Him.' Its indefiniteness is for magnification and grandeur, as if He said: He will uncover a shin of great magnitude, whose greatness is exalted and whose station is too high to have any equal, likeness, or similitude. They say: interpreting the verse as severity is not valid in any way; for the usage of people in such matters is to say: the severity was uncovered from the people, not 'it was uncovered from them,' as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word﴾ (al-Zukhruf: 50), and He said: ﴿And if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicted them of harm﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 75). So the punishment and the severity are what is uncovered, not that from which it is uncovered. Also, there the severity arises and intensifies, and it does not cease except by entry into Paradise, and there they are not summoned to prostrate; rather, they are summoned to it at the height of severity." End of quote, taken from al-Tahdhir min Mukhtasarat al-Sabuni. See also: 'Aqidat al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir by Shaykh 'Abd al-Akhir al-Ghunaymi (pp. 48, 49), and al-Tahdhir by Shaykh Bakr Abu Zayd (pp. 350–353).]] In its chain there is an unidentified man [[In A: "a suspected man".]]. And Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them﴾ means: in the Hereafter, because of their crimes and arrogance in the world. They are being repaid with the opposite of what they used to be. When they were summoned to prostrate in the world but refused, despite their health and soundness, they are likewise punished with being unable to do so in the Hereafter. When the Lord, mighty and majestic is He, is manifested, the believers will prostrate to Him, and none of the disbelievers or hypocrites will be able to prostrate. Rather, the back of each one of them will become one solid plate. Whenever one of them wants to prostrate, he falls onto his back, the reverse of prostration, just as they used to be in the world, in contrast to what the believers are upon.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So leave Me with the one who denies this discourse﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. This is a severe threat, meaning: leave Me to deal with him, between Me and him. I know how to lead him step by step, and I give him respite in his error, then I seize him with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. Therefore He said: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾, meaning: while they are not aware, rather they believe that this is a favour from Allah, while in reality it is a humiliation, as He said: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children is a hastening for them of good things? Nay, they do not perceive﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 55, 56), and He said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾ (al-An'am: 44). Therefore He said here: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: I will delay them, give them time, and extend them, and that is from My plan and My scheme against them. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: great against those who oppose My command, deny My messengers, and dare to disobey Me.

In the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then he recited: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ (Hud: 102). [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4686), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2583), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His statement: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are burdened with debt? Or is the unseen with them, so they write it down?﴾ Their explanation has passed in the surah al-Tur [[In M: "in surah al-Nur".]] [[At the explanation of the two verses: 40, 41.]]. The meaning of that is: O Muhammad, you call them to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, without a payment you take from them, but rather you hope for the reward of that with Allah, mighty and majestic is He, while they deny what you have brought them, out of pure ignorance, disbelief, and obstinacy.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the first hour that will occur on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujahid: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "The severity of the matter and its seriousness."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas his statement: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that it is "the severe and dreadful matter of terror on the Day of Resurrection."

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas his statement: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "When the matter is uncovered and deeds are displayed. Its uncovering is entry into the Hereafter, and the uncovering of the matter from it." Likewise al-Dahhak and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir cited all of this, then said:

Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me: Harun ibn 'Umar al-Makhzumi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abu Sa'id Rawh ibn Janah narrated to us, from a client of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said regarding ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾: "From a great light, they will fall down prostrating to Him."

Abu Ya'la also narrated it, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, with the same chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/27) and Musnad Abi Ya'la (13/269).

Note: Some people thought that Ibn Kathir took here the path of ta'wil (figurative interpretation) regarding the attribute of the shin, and this is a mistaken understanding. This is because Ibn Kathir explained this verse by the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, then mentioned what was said about this verse. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim spoke about this verse with an excellent discussion. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Sawa'iq al-Mursalah (1/252, 253): "The Companions differed in the interpretation of this verse: is the meaning the uncovering of severity, or is the meaning that the Lord, exalted is He, uncovers His shin? Nothing is reported from the Companions and Successors as a dispute about whether it is among the attributes or not, outside this context. Nothing in the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that this is an attribute of Allah, because He, glorified is He, did not attribute the shin to Himself, but mentioned it bare, without attribution and indefinite. Those who affirmed that it is an attribute, like the two hands and the finger, did not take that from the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, but affirmed it by the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, which is agreed upon as sound, the long hadith of intercession, in which is: 'Then the Lord will uncover His shin, and they will fall down prostrating to Him.' Whoever interprets the verse as that says: the statement of the Exalted, 'On the Day when the shin will be laid bare and they will be summoned to prostrate' (al-Qalam: 42), corresponds to the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Then He will uncover His shin, and they will fall down prostrating to Him.' Its indefiniteness is for magnification and grandeur, as if He said: He will uncover a shin of great magnitude, whose greatness is exalted and whose station is too high to have any equal, likeness, or similitude. They say: interpreting the verse as severity is not valid in any way; for the usage of people in such matters is to say: the severity was uncovered from the people, not 'it was uncovered from them,' as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word﴾ (al-Zukhruf: 50), and He said: ﴿And if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicted them of harm﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 75). So the punishment and the severity are what is uncovered, not that from which it is uncovered. Also, there the severity arises and intensifies, and it does not cease except by entry into Paradise, and there they are not summoned to prostrate; rather, they are summoned to it at the height of severity." End of quote, taken from al-Tahdhir min Mukhtasarat al-Sabuni. See also: 'Aqidat al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir by Shaykh 'Abd al-Akhir al-Ghunaymi (pp. 48, 49), and al-Tahdhir by Shaykh Bakr Abu Zayd (pp. 350–353).]] In its chain there is an unidentified man [[In A: "a suspected man".]]. And Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them﴾ means: in the Hereafter, because of their crimes and arrogance in the world. They are being repaid with the opposite of what they used to be. When they were summoned to prostrate in the world but refused, despite their health and soundness, they are likewise punished with being unable to do so in the Hereafter. When the Lord, mighty and majestic is He, is manifested, the believers will prostrate to Him, and none of the disbelievers or hypocrites will be able to prostrate. Rather, the back of each one of them will become one solid plate. Whenever one of them wants to prostrate, he falls onto his back, the reverse of prostration, just as they used to be in the world, in contrast to what the believers are upon.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So leave Me with the one who denies this discourse﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. This is a severe threat, meaning: leave Me to deal with him, between Me and him. I know how to lead him step by step, and I give him respite in his error, then I seize him with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. Therefore He said: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾, meaning: while they are not aware, rather they believe that this is a favour from Allah, while in reality it is a humiliation, as He said: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children is a hastening for them of good things? Nay, they do not perceive﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 55, 56), and He said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾ (al-An'am: 44). Therefore He said here: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: I will delay them, give them time, and extend them, and that is from My plan and My scheme against them. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: great against those who oppose My command, deny My messengers, and dare to disobey Me.

In the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then he recited: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ (Hud: 102). [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4686), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2583), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His statement: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are burdened with debt? Or is the unseen with them, so they write it down?﴾ Their explanation has passed in the surah al-Tur [[In M: "in surah al-Nur".]] [[At the explanation of the two verses: 40, 41.]]. The meaning of that is: O Muhammad, you call them to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, without a payment you take from them, but rather you hope for the reward of that with Allah, mighty and majestic is He, while they deny what you have brought them, out of pure ignorance, disbelief, and obstinacy.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 68, verses 42–47:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) with Him [[In M: "with their Lord".]] are Gardens of Bliss, He explained when that will take place and occur, saying: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare, and they will be summoned to prostrate, but they will not be able to﴾. He means: the Day of Resurrection, and what will occur in it of terrors, convulsions, trials, tests, and great matters. Al-Bukhari said here:

Adam narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. There will remain those who used to prostrate in the world for show and reputation, and they will go to prostrate, but their backs will become one solid plate." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4919).]]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs and in other works through various chains, with different wordings. It is a long, well-known hadith. [[It is the hadith of intercession, and its full text and wording were mentioned earlier in the tafsir of the first surah of al-Isra'.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Usamah ibn Zayd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "It is a day of distress and severity." Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud (or Ibn 'Abbas; the doubt is from Ibn Jarir) regarding: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be laid bare﴾, that he said: "About a great matter," like the saying of the poet:

"And war stood up among us upon its shin."  [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (29/24).]]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 68, verses 48–52 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, with the harm your people inflict upon you and their denial. Indeed, Allah will grant you victory over them and will make the final outcome favorable to you and to your followers, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Dhu'n-Nun, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, when he went away in anger at his people. So there befell him what befell him: he boarded a ship, was swallowed by the fish, the fish carried him off into the seas and the darkness of the deep waters, and he heard the glorification of the sea and all that is in it, glorifying the Most High, the Powerful, whose decree that has been issued cannot be turned back. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. Allah said: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [as-Saffat: 143–144]. Here He says: ﴿when he called out while he was suppressed [with grief]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and as-Suddi said: "meaning, he was distressed." 'Ata al-Khurasani and Abu Malik said: "meaning, he was afflicted."

We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said, ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, the words rose up and encircled the Throne. The angels said: "O Lord, this is a weak voice coming from a strange land, and it is recognizable." Allah said: "Do you not recognize it?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Yunus." They said: "O Lord, your servant whose good deeds have always been raised for him and whose supplications are answered?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, so that You rescue him from affliction?" So Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open shore. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not appropriate for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri [[Al-Musnad (1/390) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4603).]], and it is in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4631) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2376).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿would slip you﴾ means they would pierce you with their eyes, that is, they would harm you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you out of their hatred for you, were it not for Allah's protection of you and His guarding of you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye ('ayn) is real and has real effect, by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as numerous hadiths have been related through many different chains confirming this.

The hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us (ḥ). And al-'Abbas al-'Anbari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sharik informed us, from al-'Abbas ibn Dhurayh, from ash-Sha'bi, (al-'Abbas said: from Anas), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah (incantation for healing) except for the evil eye, or a sting, or bleeding that does not stop." Al-'Abbas did not mention the evil eye. This is the wording of Sulayman [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3889).]].

The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a sting" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3513).]].

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Husayn ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion), and it contains a story [[Sahih Muslim, no. (220).]]. Shu'bah also narrated it from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as at-Tirmidhi said [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi (4/345).]]. Al-Imam al-Bukhari narrated this hadith through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, Abu Dawud through the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal, and at-Tirmidhi through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. All three narrated it from Husayn, from 'Amir, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, as a mawquf [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5705); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3884); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2075).]].

The hadith of Abu Jundub ibn Junadah: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah ibn al-Birind as-Sami narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Abi Dubay narrated to us, from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the evil eye causes a man to fall by the permission of Allah, so he rises up shaved (bald?), then falls down from it." Its isnad is gharib (rare), and they did not narrate it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of Abu Ya'la, but in it there is: Ibrahim, from Daylam, from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr, so Abu Harb is dropped. The explanation of that will come from Ibn 'Adi's words. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/146) through the chain of Yunus ibn Muhammad, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of as-Salt ibn Mas'ud, both from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Wahb, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr. Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is narrated by Daylam from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, and I think the error is in the narration of as-Salt, where he said: 'from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan.' Perhaps Abu Harb is Mihjan."]].

The hadith of Habis at-Tamimi: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us, Harb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Hayyah ibn Habis at-Tamimi narrated to me, that his father informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no harm in the hamma (a type of vermin or a poisonous insect), the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen (al-fa'l)" [[Al-Musnad (5/70). In manuscript m: "al-tayr" (the omen), and in manuscript a: "al-zann" (the suspicion).]].

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from Abu Ghassan Yahya ibn Kathir, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with it. Then he said: "gharib." He said: Shayban narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah ibn Habis, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Hasan ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Shayban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah, who narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in the hamma, the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen" [[Al-Musnad (5/70).]].

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Duwayd, Isma'il ibn Thawban narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real, it brings down the one who is shaved (bald?)" [[Al-Musnad (1/274).]]. Gharib.

Another chain: Muslim said in his Sahih: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the decree, the evil eye would have preceded it. And when you are asked to wash (from the evil eye), then wash." Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2188).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every envious evil eye." And he said: "Thus Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ishaq and Isma'il, peace be upon them."

Al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of al-Minhal, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3371); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4737); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2060); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10844); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3525).]].

The hadith of Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: 'I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as delicate as a hidden maiden's.' Shortly afterward, Sahl was struck down, and he was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was said to him: 'Attend to Sahl, he has fallen.' He said: 'Whom do you suspect of this?' They said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah.' He said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees in his brother something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing for him.' Then he called for water and commanded 'Amir to perform ablution, washing his face, his two hands up to the elbows, his two knees, and the inner part of his waist-wrap, and he commanded that the water be poured over him."

Sufyan said: Ma'mar said, from az-Zuhri: "And he commanded that the vessel be overturned from behind him" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3509).]].

An-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both from az-Zuhri, with it. And through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah also, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah: "and the vessel is overturned from behind him." And through the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, with it. And through the hadith of Malik also, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, with it [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7617–7619).]].

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eyes of the jinn and the evil eyes of mankind. When al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two surahs of the Qur'an) were revealed, he took hold of them and left aside whatever else.

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud al-Jurayri, with it [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3511); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2058); Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/271).]]. At-Tirmidhi said: "hasan" (good).

Another hadith from him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to me, Abu Nadrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, have you been unwell?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and every eye, may He heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you" [[Al-Musnad (3/28).]].

He narrated it also from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Warith, the same. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/56); Sahih Muslim, no. (2186); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (975); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10843); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3523).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, or Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and Jibril came to him and said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from every envious person and evil eye, and may Allah heal you" [[Al-Musnad (3/75).]].

He also narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman at-Tufawi, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]].

Abu Zur'ah ar-Razi said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated from his father, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Nadrah, and from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are sahih (sound).

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Indeed, the evil eye is real'" [[Al-Musnad (2/318).]].

They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) both narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2187).]].

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Mudarib ibn Hazn, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with the same wording. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Thawr (meaning Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, from Makhul, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real, and the devil attends it, and the envy of the son of Adam." [[al-Musnad (2/439).]]

Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurayrah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah say, "Bad omen is in three: the house, the horse and the woman"? He said: I said: Then I would be attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something he did not say! Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of omens is good omen (fa'l), and the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (2/289).]]

The hadith of Asma' bint 'Umays: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, who said: Asma' said: O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye; shall I seek a remedy (istirqa') for them? He said: "Yes. For if anything could outstrip the decree (qadr), the evil eye would have outstripped it." [[Ibid.]]

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (6/438); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]] Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from Asma' bint 'Umays, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7537.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

The hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Ibn Majah said: 'Ali ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to seek a remedy (istirqa') for the evil eye. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, with the same chain. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan and Mis'ar, both from Ma'bad, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5738; Sahih Muslim, no. 2195.]]

Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Waqid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek refuge in Allah, for the soul (nafs) is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3508. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/134): "In this chain there is some weakness (maqal)."]]

Abu Dawud said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who had caused the evil eye (al-'a'in) used to be commanded to perform ablution, and water from it would be washed over the one afflicted (al-ma'in). [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3880.]]

The hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways [[In M: "Abu Idris".]] narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and they travelled with him toward Makkah, until when they were at Shi'b al-Kharrar (from al-Juhfah), Sahl ibn Hunayf bathed, and he was a fair-skinned man of good build and complexion. 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b, saw him while he was bathing and said: "I have never seen anything like today, nor skin so concealed (jild mukhabba'ah)!" Sahl then collapsed (lubit). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, would you come to Sahl? By Allah, he cannot raise his head, and he does not regain consciousness." He said: "Do you suspect anyone of causing it?" They said: "'Amir ibn Rabi'ah looked at him." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Amir and rebuked him severely, saying: "Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not, when you saw something that pleased you, invoke blessing (barak)?" Then he said to him: "Bathe for him." So 'Amir washed his face, his two hands, his two elbows, his two knees, the tips of his two feet and the inner edge of his waist-wrap in a vessel, and then that water was poured over him, poured by a man over his head and back from behind, and then the vessel was overturned behind him. He did this, and Sahl went out with the people, with no harm in him. [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of 'Amir: Waki' narrated to us, my father (Waki's father) narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Hind ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf set out wanting to bathe. He said: They went seeking a place with a covering (al-khamr) for bathing. He said: 'Amir put down a woollen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and struck him with my eye (fa-asabtuhu bi-'aynī), and he went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling (far'qa) from him in the water, so I came to him and called to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: Then he came walking and entered the water, as if I were looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: Then he struck his chest with his hand and said: "O Allah, turn away from him its heat, its cold and its affliction (wasab)." He said: Then he stood up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When any of you sees in his brother, or in himself, or in his property, something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing (fal-yubarrik), for the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of Jabir: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl al-Ansari narrated to us, he is called Ibn al-Daji', the companion (daji') of Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Most of my ummah die after the Book of Allah, His decree and His divine decree (qadr), by way of souls (bi-al-anfus)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3052 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/106): "Its narrators are the narrators of the sahih, except Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr, who is trustworthy (thiqah)."]]

Al-Bazzar said: He means the evil eye. He said: We do not know this hadith to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this chain.

I say: Rather, it has been narrated by another route from Jabir. The hafiz Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Munthir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned it in his book al-'Aja'ib, which contains noble and strange benefits: Al-Rahawi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real; it brings a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot. Indeed, most of the destruction of my ummah is from the evil eye." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/185) through Rahim, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Lahbi, with the same wording, and said: [not preserved (ghayr mahfuz)]. 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali is weak (afanah); Ahmad said: he narrates unfamiliar (munkar) hadiths from Jabir.]]

Then he narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye may bring a man into the grave, and bring a camel into the cooking pot." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/408), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/90), through several routes from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub with the same wording. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of al-Thawri; Mu'awiyah alone narrated it." Ibn 'Adi said the same.]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Hisham ibn Abi Ruqayyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion ('adwa), no bad omen (tiyarah), no hamah, and no envy (hasad), and the evil eye is real." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[al-Musnad (2/222).]]

A hadith from 'Ali: The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Khaythamah ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Kashuri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Basri narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him distressed, and said: "O Muhammad, what is this distress I see in your face?" He said: "Al-Hasan and al-Husayn have been afflicted by the evil eye." He said: "The evil eye has spoken the truth, for the evil eye is real. Why did you not seek refuge (ta'awwadhta) for them with these words?" He said: "And what are they, O Jibril?" He said: Say: "O Allah, Lord of the great authority, possessor of ancient favour, possessor of the noble face, Guardian of the perfect words and the answered supplications, heal al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind." So the Prophet ﷺ said it, and they both got up playing before him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek refuge for yourselves, your women and your children with this charm (ta'widh), for those who seek refuge have never sought refuge with its like."

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Hayati alone narrated it, from the people of Tustar. [[In Tarikh Dimashq: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hanzali", and in Kanz al-'Ummal: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khatibi"; I have not determined the correct form, and Allah knows best.]] Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in the biography of "Tarrad ibn al-Husayn" in his Tarikh. [[Tarikh Dimashq (8/503, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, they belittle him with their eyes and harm him with their tongues, and they say: ﴿Indeed, he is mad﴾, because of his bringing the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 68, verses 48–52 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, with the harm your people inflict upon you and their denial. Indeed, Allah will grant you victory over them and will make the final outcome favorable to you and to your followers, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Dhu'n-Nun, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, when he went away in anger at his people. So there befell him what befell him: he boarded a ship, was swallowed by the fish, the fish carried him off into the seas and the darkness of the deep waters, and he heard the glorification of the sea and all that is in it, glorifying the Most High, the Powerful, whose decree that has been issued cannot be turned back. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. Allah said: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [as-Saffat: 143–144]. Here He says: ﴿when he called out while he was suppressed [with grief]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and as-Suddi said: "meaning, he was distressed." 'Ata al-Khurasani and Abu Malik said: "meaning, he was afflicted."

We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said, ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, the words rose up and encircled the Throne. The angels said: "O Lord, this is a weak voice coming from a strange land, and it is recognizable." Allah said: "Do you not recognize it?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Yunus." They said: "O Lord, your servant whose good deeds have always been raised for him and whose supplications are answered?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, so that You rescue him from affliction?" So Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open shore. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not appropriate for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri [[Al-Musnad (1/390) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4603).]], and it is in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4631) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2376).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿would slip you﴾ means they would pierce you with their eyes, that is, they would harm you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you out of their hatred for you, were it not for Allah's protection of you and His guarding of you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye ('ayn) is real and has real effect, by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as numerous hadiths have been related through many different chains confirming this.

The hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us (ḥ). And al-'Abbas al-'Anbari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sharik informed us, from al-'Abbas ibn Dhurayh, from ash-Sha'bi, (al-'Abbas said: from Anas), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah (incantation for healing) except for the evil eye, or a sting, or bleeding that does not stop." Al-'Abbas did not mention the evil eye. This is the wording of Sulayman [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3889).]].

The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a sting" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3513).]].

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Husayn ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion), and it contains a story [[Sahih Muslim, no. (220).]]. Shu'bah also narrated it from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as at-Tirmidhi said [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi (4/345).]]. Al-Imam al-Bukhari narrated this hadith through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, Abu Dawud through the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal, and at-Tirmidhi through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. All three narrated it from Husayn, from 'Amir, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, as a mawquf [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5705); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3884); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2075).]].

The hadith of Abu Jundub ibn Junadah: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah ibn al-Birind as-Sami narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Abi Dubay narrated to us, from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the evil eye causes a man to fall by the permission of Allah, so he rises up shaved (bald?), then falls down from it." Its isnad is gharib (rare), and they did not narrate it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of Abu Ya'la, but in it there is: Ibrahim, from Daylam, from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr, so Abu Harb is dropped. The explanation of that will come from Ibn 'Adi's words. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/146) through the chain of Yunus ibn Muhammad, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of as-Salt ibn Mas'ud, both from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Wahb, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr. Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is narrated by Daylam from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, and I think the error is in the narration of as-Salt, where he said: 'from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan.' Perhaps Abu Harb is Mihjan."]].

The hadith of Habis at-Tamimi: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us, Harb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Hayyah ibn Habis at-Tamimi narrated to me, that his father informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no harm in the hamma (a type of vermin or a poisonous insect), the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen (al-fa'l)" [[Al-Musnad (5/70). In manuscript m: "al-tayr" (the omen), and in manuscript a: "al-zann" (the suspicion).]].

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from Abu Ghassan Yahya ibn Kathir, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with it. Then he said: "gharib." He said: Shayban narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah ibn Habis, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Hasan ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Shayban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah, who narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in the hamma, the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen" [[Al-Musnad (5/70).]].

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Duwayd, Isma'il ibn Thawban narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real, it brings down the one who is shaved (bald?)" [[Al-Musnad (1/274).]]. Gharib.

Another chain: Muslim said in his Sahih: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the decree, the evil eye would have preceded it. And when you are asked to wash (from the evil eye), then wash." Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2188).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every envious evil eye." And he said: "Thus Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ishaq and Isma'il, peace be upon them."

Al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of al-Minhal, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3371); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4737); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2060); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10844); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3525).]].

The hadith of Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: 'I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as delicate as a hidden maiden's.' Shortly afterward, Sahl was struck down, and he was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was said to him: 'Attend to Sahl, he has fallen.' He said: 'Whom do you suspect of this?' They said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah.' He said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees in his brother something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing for him.' Then he called for water and commanded 'Amir to perform ablution, washing his face, his two hands up to the elbows, his two knees, and the inner part of his waist-wrap, and he commanded that the water be poured over him."

Sufyan said: Ma'mar said, from az-Zuhri: "And he commanded that the vessel be overturned from behind him" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3509).]].

An-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both from az-Zuhri, with it. And through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah also, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah: "and the vessel is overturned from behind him." And through the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, with it. And through the hadith of Malik also, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, with it [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7617–7619).]].

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eyes of the jinn and the evil eyes of mankind. When al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two surahs of the Qur'an) were revealed, he took hold of them and left aside whatever else.

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud al-Jurayri, with it [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3511); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2058); Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/271).]]. At-Tirmidhi said: "hasan" (good).

Another hadith from him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to me, Abu Nadrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, have you been unwell?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and every eye, may He heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you" [[Al-Musnad (3/28).]].

He narrated it also from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Warith, the same. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/56); Sahih Muslim, no. (2186); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (975); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10843); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3523).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, or Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and Jibril came to him and said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from every envious person and evil eye, and may Allah heal you" [[Al-Musnad (3/75).]].

He also narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman at-Tufawi, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]].

Abu Zur'ah ar-Razi said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated from his father, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Nadrah, and from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are sahih (sound).

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Indeed, the evil eye is real'" [[Al-Musnad (2/318).]].

They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) both narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2187).]].

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Mudarib ibn Hazn, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with the same wording. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Thawr (meaning Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, from Makhul, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real, and the devil attends it, and the envy of the son of Adam." [[al-Musnad (2/439).]]

Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurayrah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah say, "Bad omen is in three: the house, the horse and the woman"? He said: I said: Then I would be attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something he did not say! Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of omens is good omen (fa'l), and the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (2/289).]]

The hadith of Asma' bint 'Umays: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, who said: Asma' said: O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye; shall I seek a remedy (istirqa') for them? He said: "Yes. For if anything could outstrip the decree (qadr), the evil eye would have outstripped it." [[Ibid.]]

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain.
