[[al-Musnad (6/438); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]] Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from Asma' bint 'Umays, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7537.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

The hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Ibn Majah said: 'Ali ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to seek a remedy (istirqa') for the evil eye. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, with the same chain. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan and Mis'ar, both from Ma'bad, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5738; Sahih Muslim, no. 2195.]]

Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Waqid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek refuge in Allah, for the soul (nafs) is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3508. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/134): "In this chain there is some weakness (maqal)."]]

Abu Dawud said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who had caused the evil eye (al-'a'in) used to be commanded to perform ablution, and water from it would be washed over the one afflicted (al-ma'in). [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3880.]]

The hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways [[In M: "Abu Idris".]] narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and they travelled with him toward Makkah, until when they were at Shi'b al-Kharrar (from al-Juhfah), Sahl ibn Hunayf bathed, and he was a fair-skinned man of good build and complexion. 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b, saw him while he was bathing and said: "I have never seen anything like today, nor skin so concealed (jild mukhabba'ah)!" Sahl then collapsed (lubit). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, would you come to Sahl? By Allah, he cannot raise his head, and he does not regain consciousness." He said: "Do you suspect anyone of causing it?" They said: "'Amir ibn Rabi'ah looked at him." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Amir and rebuked him severely, saying: "Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not, when you saw something that pleased you, invoke blessing (barak)?" Then he said to him: "Bathe for him." So 'Amir washed his face, his two hands, his two elbows, his two knees, the tips of his two feet and the inner edge of his waist-wrap in a vessel, and then that water was poured over him, poured by a man over his head and back from behind, and then the vessel was overturned behind him. He did this, and Sahl went out with the people, with no harm in him. [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of 'Amir: Waki' narrated to us, my father (Waki's father) narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Hind ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf set out wanting to bathe. He said: They went seeking a place with a covering (al-khamr) for bathing. He said: 'Amir put down a woollen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and struck him with my eye (fa-asabtuhu bi-'aynī), and he went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling (far'qa) from him in the water, so I came to him and called to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: Then he came walking and entered the water, as if I were looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: Then he struck his chest with his hand and said: "O Allah, turn away from him its heat, its cold and its affliction (wasab)." He said: Then he stood up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When any of you sees in his brother, or in himself, or in his property, something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing (fal-yubarrik), for the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of Jabir: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl al-Ansari narrated to us, he is called Ibn al-Daji', the companion (daji') of Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Most of my ummah die after the Book of Allah, His decree and His divine decree (qadr), by way of souls (bi-al-anfus)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3052 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/106): "Its narrators are the narrators of the sahih, except Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr, who is trustworthy (thiqah)."]]

Al-Bazzar said: He means the evil eye. He said: We do not know this hadith to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this chain.

I say: Rather, it has been narrated by another route from Jabir. The hafiz Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Munthir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned it in his book al-'Aja'ib, which contains noble and strange benefits: Al-Rahawi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real; it brings a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot. Indeed, most of the destruction of my ummah is from the evil eye." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/185) through Rahim, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Lahbi, with the same wording, and said: [not preserved (ghayr mahfuz)]. 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali is weak (afanah); Ahmad said: he narrates unfamiliar (munkar) hadiths from Jabir.]]

Then he narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye may bring a man into the grave, and bring a camel into the cooking pot." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/408), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/90), through several routes from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub with the same wording. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of al-Thawri; Mu'awiyah alone narrated it." Ibn 'Adi said the same.]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Hisham ibn Abi Ruqayyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion ('adwa), no bad omen (tiyarah), no hamah, and no envy (hasad), and the evil eye is real." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[al-Musnad (2/222).]]

A hadith from 'Ali: The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Khaythamah ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Kashuri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Basri narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him distressed, and said: "O Muhammad, what is this distress I see in your face?" He said: "Al-Hasan and al-Husayn have been afflicted by the evil eye." He said: "The evil eye has spoken the truth, for the evil eye is real. Why did you not seek refuge (ta'awwadhta) for them with these words?" He said: "And what are they, O Jibril?" He said: Say: "O Allah, Lord of the great authority, possessor of ancient favour, possessor of the noble face, Guardian of the perfect words and the answered supplications, heal al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind." So the Prophet ﷺ said it, and they both got up playing before him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek refuge for yourselves, your women and your children with this charm (ta'widh), for those who seek refuge have never sought refuge with its like."

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Hayati alone narrated it, from the people of Tustar. [[In Tarikh Dimashq: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hanzali", and in Kanz al-'Ummal: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khatibi"; I have not determined the correct form, and Allah knows best.]] Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in the biography of "Tarrad ibn al-Husayn" in his Tarikh. [[Tarikh Dimashq (8/503, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, they belittle him with their eyes and harm him with their tongues, and they say: ﴿Indeed, he is mad﴾, because of his bringing the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 68, verses 48–52 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, with the harm your people inflict upon you and their denial. Indeed, Allah will grant you victory over them and will make the final outcome favorable to you and to your followers, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Dhu'n-Nun, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, when he went away in anger at his people. So there befell him what befell him: he boarded a ship, was swallowed by the fish, the fish carried him off into the seas and the darkness of the deep waters, and he heard the glorification of the sea and all that is in it, glorifying the Most High, the Powerful, whose decree that has been issued cannot be turned back. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. Allah said: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [as-Saffat: 143–144]. Here He says: ﴿when he called out while he was suppressed [with grief]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and as-Suddi said: "meaning, he was distressed." 'Ata al-Khurasani and Abu Malik said: "meaning, he was afflicted."

We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said, ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, the words rose up and encircled the Throne. The angels said: "O Lord, this is a weak voice coming from a strange land, and it is recognizable." Allah said: "Do you not recognize it?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Yunus." They said: "O Lord, your servant whose good deeds have always been raised for him and whose supplications are answered?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, so that You rescue him from affliction?" So Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open shore. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not appropriate for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri [[Al-Musnad (1/390) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4603).]], and it is in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4631) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2376).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿would slip you﴾ means they would pierce you with their eyes, that is, they would harm you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you out of their hatred for you, were it not for Allah's protection of you and His guarding of you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye ('ayn) is real and has real effect, by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as numerous hadiths have been related through many different chains confirming this.

The hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us (ḥ). And al-'Abbas al-'Anbari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sharik informed us, from al-'Abbas ibn Dhurayh, from ash-Sha'bi, (al-'Abbas said: from Anas), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah (incantation for healing) except for the evil eye, or a sting, or bleeding that does not stop." Al-'Abbas did not mention the evil eye. This is the wording of Sulayman [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3889).]].

The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a sting" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3513).]].

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Husayn ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion), and it contains a story [[Sahih Muslim, no. (220).]]. Shu'bah also narrated it from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as at-Tirmidhi said [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi (4/345).]]. Al-Imam al-Bukhari narrated this hadith through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, Abu Dawud through the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal, and at-Tirmidhi through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. All three narrated it from Husayn, from 'Amir, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, as a mawquf [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5705); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3884); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2075).]].

The hadith of Abu Jundub ibn Junadah: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah ibn al-Birind as-Sami narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Abi Dubay narrated to us, from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the evil eye causes a man to fall by the permission of Allah, so he rises up shaved (bald?), then falls down from it." Its isnad is gharib (rare), and they did not narrate it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of Abu Ya'la, but in it there is: Ibrahim, from Daylam, from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr, so Abu Harb is dropped. The explanation of that will come from Ibn 'Adi's words. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/146) through the chain of Yunus ibn Muhammad, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of as-Salt ibn Mas'ud, both from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Wahb, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr. Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is narrated by Daylam from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, and I think the error is in the narration of as-Salt, where he said: 'from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan.' Perhaps Abu Harb is Mihjan."]].

The hadith of Habis at-Tamimi: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us, Harb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Hayyah ibn Habis at-Tamimi narrated to me, that his father informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no harm in the hamma (a type of vermin or a poisonous insect), the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen (al-fa'l)" [[Al-Musnad (5/70). In manuscript m: "al-tayr" (the omen), and in manuscript a: "al-zann" (the suspicion).]].

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from Abu Ghassan Yahya ibn Kathir, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with it. Then he said: "gharib." He said: Shayban narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah ibn Habis, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Hasan ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Shayban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah, who narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in the hamma, the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen" [[Al-Musnad (5/70).]].

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Duwayd, Isma'il ibn Thawban narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real, it brings down the one who is shaved (bald?)" [[Al-Musnad (1/274).]]. Gharib.

Another chain: Muslim said in his Sahih: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the decree, the evil eye would have preceded it. And when you are asked to wash (from the evil eye), then wash." Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2188).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every envious evil eye." And he said: "Thus Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ishaq and Isma'il, peace be upon them."

Al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of al-Minhal, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3371); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4737); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2060); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10844); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3525).]].

The hadith of Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: 'I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as delicate as a hidden maiden's.' Shortly afterward, Sahl was struck down, and he was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was said to him: 'Attend to Sahl, he has fallen.' He said: 'Whom do you suspect of this?' They said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah.' He said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees in his brother something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing for him.' Then he called for water and commanded 'Amir to perform ablution, washing his face, his two hands up to the elbows, his two knees, and the inner part of his waist-wrap, and he commanded that the water be poured over him."

Sufyan said: Ma'mar said, from az-Zuhri: "And he commanded that the vessel be overturned from behind him" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3509).]].

An-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both from az-Zuhri, with it. And through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah also, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah: "and the vessel is overturned from behind him." And through the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, with it. And through the hadith of Malik also, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, with it [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7617–7619).]].

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eyes of the jinn and the evil eyes of mankind. When al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two surahs of the Qur'an) were revealed, he took hold of them and left aside whatever else.

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud al-Jurayri, with it [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3511); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2058); Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/271).]]. At-Tirmidhi said: "hasan" (good).

Another hadith from him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to me, Abu Nadrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, have you been unwell?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and every eye, may He heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you" [[Al-Musnad (3/28).]].

He narrated it also from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Warith, the same. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/56); Sahih Muslim, no. (2186); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (975); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10843); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3523).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, or Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and Jibril came to him and said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from every envious person and evil eye, and may Allah heal you" [[Al-Musnad (3/75).]].

He also narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman at-Tufawi, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]].

Abu Zur'ah ar-Razi said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated from his father, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Nadrah, and from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are sahih (sound).

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Indeed, the evil eye is real'" [[Al-Musnad (2/318).]].

They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) both narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2187).]].

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Mudarib ibn Hazn, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with the same wording. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Thawr (meaning Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, from Makhul, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real, and the devil attends it, and the envy of the son of Adam." [[al-Musnad (2/439).]]

Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurayrah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah say, "Bad omen is in three: the house, the horse and the woman"? He said: I said: Then I would be attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something he did not say! Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of omens is good omen (fa'l), and the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (2/289).]]

The hadith of Asma' bint 'Umays: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, who said: Asma' said: O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye; shall I seek a remedy (istirqa') for them? He said: "Yes. For if anything could outstrip the decree (qadr), the evil eye would have outstripped it." [[Ibid.]]

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (6/438); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]] Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from Asma' bint 'Umays, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7537.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

The hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Ibn Majah said: 'Ali ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to seek a remedy (istirqa') for the evil eye. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, with the same chain. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan and Mis'ar, both from Ma'bad, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5738; Sahih Muslim, no. 2195.]]

Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Waqid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek refuge in Allah, for the soul (nafs) is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3508. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/134): "In this chain there is some weakness (maqal)."]]

Abu Dawud said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who had caused the evil eye (al-'a'in) used to be commanded to perform ablution, and water from it would be washed over the one afflicted (al-ma'in). [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3880.]]

The hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways [[In M: "Abu Idris".]] narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and they travelled with him toward Makkah, until when they were at Shi'b al-Kharrar (from al-Juhfah), Sahl ibn Hunayf bathed, and he was a fair-skinned man of good build and complexion. 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b, saw him while he was bathing and said: "I have never seen anything like today, nor skin so concealed (jild mukhabba'ah)!" Sahl then collapsed (lubit). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, would you come to Sahl? By Allah, he cannot raise his head, and he does not regain consciousness." He said: "Do you suspect anyone of causing it?" They said: "'Amir ibn Rabi'ah looked at him." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Amir and rebuked him severely, saying: "Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not, when you saw something that pleased you, invoke blessing (barak)?" Then he said to him: "Bathe for him." So 'Amir washed his face, his two hands, his two elbows, his two knees, the tips of his two feet and the inner edge of his waist-wrap in a vessel, and then that water was poured over him, poured by a man over his head and back from behind, and then the vessel was overturned behind him. He did this, and Sahl went out with the people, with no harm in him. [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of 'Amir: Waki' narrated to us, my father (Waki's father) narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Hind ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf set out wanting to bathe. He said: They went seeking a place with a covering (al-khamr) for bathing. He said: 'Amir put down a woollen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and struck him with my eye (fa-asabtuhu bi-'aynī), and he went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling (far'qa) from him in the water, so I came to him and called to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: Then he came walking and entered the water, as if I were looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: Then he struck his chest with his hand and said: "O Allah, turn away from him its heat, its cold and its affliction (wasab)." He said: Then he stood up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When any of you sees in his brother, or in himself, or in his property, something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing (fal-yubarrik), for the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of Jabir: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl al-Ansari narrated to us, he is called Ibn al-Daji', the companion (daji') of Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Most of my ummah die after the Book of Allah, His decree and His divine decree (qadr), by way of souls (bi-al-anfus)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3052 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/106): "Its narrators are the narrators of the sahih, except Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr, who is trustworthy (thiqah)."]]

Al-Bazzar said: He means the evil eye. He said: We do not know this hadith to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this chain.

I say: Rather, it has been narrated by another route from Jabir. The hafiz Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Munthir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned it in his book al-'Aja'ib, which contains noble and strange benefits: Al-Rahawi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real; it brings a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot. Indeed, most of the destruction of my ummah is from the evil eye." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/185) through Rahim, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Lahbi, with the same wording, and said: [not preserved (ghayr mahfuz)]. 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali is weak (afanah); Ahmad said: he narrates unfamiliar (munkar) hadiths from Jabir.]]

Then he narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye may bring a man into the grave, and bring a camel into the cooking pot." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/408), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/90), through several routes from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub with the same wording. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of al-Thawri; Mu'awiyah alone narrated it." Ibn 'Adi said the same.]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Hisham ibn Abi Ruqayyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion ('adwa), no bad omen (tiyarah), no hamah, and no envy (hasad), and the evil eye is real." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[al-Musnad (2/222).]]

A hadith from 'Ali: The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Khaythamah ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Kashuri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Basri narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him distressed, and said: "O Muhammad, what is this distress I see in your face?" He said: "Al-Hasan and al-Husayn have been afflicted by the evil eye." He said: "The evil eye has spoken the truth, for the evil eye is real. Why did you not seek refuge (ta'awwadhta) for them with these words?" He said: "And what are they, O Jibril?" He said: Say: "O Allah, Lord of the great authority, possessor of ancient favour, possessor of the noble face, Guardian of the perfect words and the answered supplications, heal al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind." So the Prophet ﷺ said it, and they both got up playing before him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek refuge for yourselves, your women and your children with this charm (ta'widh), for those who seek refuge have never sought refuge with its like."

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Hayati alone narrated it, from the people of Tustar. [[In Tarikh Dimashq: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hanzali", and in Kanz al-'Ummal: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khatibi"; I have not determined the correct form, and Allah knows best.]] Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in the biography of "Tarrad ibn al-Husayn" in his Tarikh. [[Tarikh Dimashq (8/503, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, they belittle him with their eyes and harm him with their tongues, and they say: ﴿Indeed, he is mad﴾, because of his bringing the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 68, verses 48–52 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, with the harm your people inflict upon you and their denial. Indeed, Allah will grant you victory over them and will make the final outcome favorable to you and to your followers, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Dhu'n-Nun, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, when he went away in anger at his people. So there befell him what befell him: he boarded a ship, was swallowed by the fish, the fish carried him off into the seas and the darkness of the deep waters, and he heard the glorification of the sea and all that is in it, glorifying the Most High, the Powerful, whose decree that has been issued cannot be turned back. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. Allah said: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [as-Saffat: 143–144]. Here He says: ﴿when he called out while he was suppressed [with grief]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and as-Suddi said: "meaning, he was distressed." 'Ata al-Khurasani and Abu Malik said: "meaning, he was afflicted."

We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said, ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, the words rose up and encircled the Throne. The angels said: "O Lord, this is a weak voice coming from a strange land, and it is recognizable." Allah said: "Do you not recognize it?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Yunus." They said: "O Lord, your servant whose good deeds have always been raised for him and whose supplications are answered?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, so that You rescue him from affliction?" So Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open shore. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not appropriate for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri [[Al-Musnad (1/390) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4603).]], and it is in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4631) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2376).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿would slip you﴾ means they would pierce you with their eyes, that is, they would harm you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you out of their hatred for you, were it not for Allah's protection of you and His guarding of you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye ('ayn) is real and has real effect, by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as numerous hadiths have been related through many different chains confirming this.

The hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us (ḥ). And al-'Abbas al-'Anbari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sharik informed us, from al-'Abbas ibn Dhurayh, from ash-Sha'bi, (al-'Abbas said: from Anas), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah (incantation for healing) except for the evil eye, or a sting, or bleeding that does not stop." Al-'Abbas did not mention the evil eye. This is the wording of Sulayman [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3889).]].

The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a sting" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3513).]].

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Husayn ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion), and it contains a story [[Sahih Muslim, no. (220).]]. Shu'bah also narrated it from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as at-Tirmidhi said [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi (4/345).]]. Al-Imam al-Bukhari narrated this hadith through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, Abu Dawud through the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal, and at-Tirmidhi through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. All three narrated it from Husayn, from 'Amir, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, as a mawquf [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5705); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3884); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2075).]].

The hadith of Abu Jundub ibn Junadah: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah ibn al-Birind as-Sami narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Abi Dubay narrated to us, from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the evil eye causes a man to fall by the permission of Allah, so he rises up shaved (bald?), then falls down from it." Its isnad is gharib (rare), and they did not narrate it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of Abu Ya'la, but in it there is: Ibrahim, from Daylam, from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr, so Abu Harb is dropped. The explanation of that will come from Ibn 'Adi's words. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/146) through the chain of Yunus ibn Muhammad, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of as-Salt ibn Mas'ud, both from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Wahb, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr. Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is narrated by Daylam from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, and I think the error is in the narration of as-Salt, where he said: 'from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan.' Perhaps Abu Harb is Mihjan."]].

The hadith of Habis at-Tamimi: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us, Harb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Hayyah ibn Habis at-Tamimi narrated to me, that his father informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no harm in the hamma (a type of vermin or a poisonous insect), the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen (al-fa'l)" [[Al-Musnad (5/70). In manuscript m: "al-tayr" (the omen), and in manuscript a: "al-zann" (the suspicion).]].

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from Abu Ghassan Yahya ibn Kathir, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with it. Then he said: "gharib." He said: Shayban narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah ibn Habis, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Hasan ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Shayban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah, who narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in the hamma, the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen" [[Al-Musnad (5/70).]].

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Duwayd, Isma'il ibn Thawban narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real, it brings down the one who is shaved (bald?)" [[Al-Musnad (1/274).]]. Gharib.

Another chain: Muslim said in his Sahih: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the decree, the evil eye would have preceded it. And when you are asked to wash (from the evil eye), then wash." Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2188).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every envious evil eye." And he said: "Thus Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ishaq and Isma'il, peace be upon them."

Al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of al-Minhal, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3371); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4737); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2060); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10844); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3525).]].

The hadith of Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: 'I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as delicate as a hidden maiden's.' Shortly afterward, Sahl was struck down, and he was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was said to him: 'Attend to Sahl, he has fallen.' He said: 'Whom do you suspect of this?' They said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah.' He said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees in his brother something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing for him.' Then he called for water and commanded 'Amir to perform ablution, washing his face, his two hands up to the elbows, his two knees, and the inner part of his waist-wrap, and he commanded that the water be poured over him."

Sufyan said: Ma'mar said, from az-Zuhri: "And he commanded that the vessel be overturned from behind him" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3509).]].

An-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both from az-Zuhri, with it. And through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah also, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah: "and the vessel is overturned from behind him." And through the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, with it. And through the hadith of Malik also, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, with it [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7617–7619).]].

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eyes of the jinn and the evil eyes of mankind. When al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two surahs of the Qur'an) were revealed, he took hold of them and left aside whatever else.

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud al-Jurayri, with it [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3511); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2058); Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/271).]]. At-Tirmidhi said: "hasan" (good).

Another hadith from him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to me, Abu Nadrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, have you been unwell?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and every eye, may He heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you" [[Al-Musnad (3/28).]].

He narrated it also from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Warith, the same. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/56); Sahih Muslim, no. (2186); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (975); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10843); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3523).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, or Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and Jibril came to him and said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from every envious person and evil eye, and may Allah heal you" [[Al-Musnad (3/75).]].

He also narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman at-Tufawi, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]].

Abu Zur'ah ar-Razi said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated from his father, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Nadrah, and from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are sahih (sound).

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Indeed, the evil eye is real'" [[Al-Musnad (2/318).]].

They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) both narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2187).]].

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Mudarib ibn Hazn, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with the same wording. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Thawr (meaning Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, from Makhul, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real, and the devil attends it, and the envy of the son of Adam." [[al-Musnad (2/439).]]

Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurayrah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah say, "Bad omen is in three: the house, the horse and the woman"? He said: I said: Then I would be attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something he did not say! Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of omens is good omen (fa'l), and the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (2/289).]]

The hadith of Asma' bint 'Umays: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, who said: Asma' said: O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye; shall I seek a remedy (istirqa') for them? He said: "Yes. For if anything could outstrip the decree (qadr), the evil eye would have outstripped it." [[Ibid.]]

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (6/438); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]] Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from Asma' bint 'Umays, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7537.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

The hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Ibn Majah said: 'Ali ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to seek a remedy (istirqa') for the evil eye. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, with the same chain. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan and Mis'ar, both from Ma'bad, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5738; Sahih Muslim, no. 2195.]]

Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Waqid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek refuge in Allah, for the soul (nafs) is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3508. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/134): "In this chain there is some weakness (maqal)."]]

Abu Dawud said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who had caused the evil eye (al-'a'in) used to be commanded to perform ablution, and water from it would be washed over the one afflicted (al-ma'in). [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3880.]]

The hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways [[In M: "Abu Idris".]] narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and they travelled with him toward Makkah, until when they were at Shi'b al-Kharrar (from al-Juhfah), Sahl ibn Hunayf bathed, and he was a fair-skinned man of good build and complexion. 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b, saw him while he was bathing and said: "I have never seen anything like today, nor skin so concealed (jild mukhabba'ah)!" Sahl then collapsed (lubit). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, would you come to Sahl? By Allah, he cannot raise his head, and he does not regain consciousness." He said: "Do you suspect anyone of causing it?" They said: "'Amir ibn Rabi'ah looked at him." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Amir and rebuked him severely, saying: "Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not, when you saw something that pleased you, invoke blessing (barak)?" Then he said to him: "Bathe for him." So 'Amir washed his face, his two hands, his two elbows, his two knees, the tips of his two feet and the inner edge of his waist-wrap in a vessel, and then that water was poured over him, poured by a man over his head and back from behind, and then the vessel was overturned behind him. He did this, and Sahl went out with the people, with no harm in him. [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of 'Amir: Waki' narrated to us, my father (Waki's father) narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Hind ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf set out wanting to bathe. He said: They went seeking a place with a covering (al-khamr) for bathing. He said: 'Amir put down a woollen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and struck him with my eye (fa-asabtuhu bi-'aynī), and he went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling (far'qa) from him in the water, so I came to him and called to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: Then he came walking and entered the water, as if I were looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: Then he struck his chest with his hand and said: "O Allah, turn away from him its heat, its cold and its affliction (wasab)." He said: Then he stood up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When any of you sees in his brother, or in himself, or in his property, something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing (fal-yubarrik), for the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of Jabir: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl al-Ansari narrated to us, he is called Ibn al-Daji', the companion (daji') of Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Most of my ummah die after the Book of Allah, His decree and His divine decree (qadr), by way of souls (bi-al-anfus)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3052 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/106): "Its narrators are the narrators of the sahih, except Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr, who is trustworthy (thiqah)."]]

Al-Bazzar said: He means the evil eye. He said: We do not know this hadith to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this chain.

I say: Rather, it has been narrated by another route from Jabir. The hafiz Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Munthir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned it in his book al-'Aja'ib, which contains noble and strange benefits: Al-Rahawi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real; it brings a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot. Indeed, most of the destruction of my ummah is from the evil eye." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/185) through Rahim, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Lahbi, with the same wording, and said: [not preserved (ghayr mahfuz)]. 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali is weak (afanah); Ahmad said: he narrates unfamiliar (munkar) hadiths from Jabir.]]

Then he narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye may bring a man into the grave, and bring a camel into the cooking pot." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/408), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/90), through several routes from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub with the same wording. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of al-Thawri; Mu'awiyah alone narrated it." Ibn 'Adi said the same.]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Hisham ibn Abi Ruqayyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion ('adwa), no bad omen (tiyarah), no hamah, and no envy (hasad), and the evil eye is real." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[al-Musnad (2/222).]]

A hadith from 'Ali: The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Khaythamah ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Kashuri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Basri narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him distressed, and said: "O Muhammad, what is this distress I see in your face?" He said: "Al-Hasan and al-Husayn have been afflicted by the evil eye." He said: "The evil eye has spoken the truth, for the evil eye is real. Why did you not seek refuge (ta'awwadhta) for them with these words?" He said: "And what are they, O Jibril?" He said: Say: "O Allah, Lord of the great authority, possessor of ancient favour, possessor of the noble face, Guardian of the perfect words and the answered supplications, heal al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind." So the Prophet ﷺ said it, and they both got up playing before him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek refuge for yourselves, your women and your children with this charm (ta'widh), for those who seek refuge have never sought refuge with its like."

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Hayati alone narrated it, from the people of Tustar. [[In Tarikh Dimashq: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hanzali", and in Kanz al-'Ummal: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khatibi"; I have not determined the correct form, and Allah knows best.]] Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in the biography of "Tarrad ibn al-Husayn" in his Tarikh. [[Tarikh Dimashq (8/503, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, they belittle him with their eyes and harm him with their tongues, and they say: ﴿Indeed, he is mad﴾, because of his bringing the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 68, verses 48–52 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, with the harm your people inflict upon you and their denial. Indeed, Allah will grant you victory over them and will make the final outcome favorable to you and to your followers, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Dhu'n-Nun, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, when he went away in anger at his people. So there befell him what befell him: he boarded a ship, was swallowed by the fish, the fish carried him off into the seas and the darkness of the deep waters, and he heard the glorification of the sea and all that is in it, glorifying the Most High, the Powerful, whose decree that has been issued cannot be turned back. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 87]. Allah said: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [as-Saffat: 143–144]. Here He says: ﴿when he called out while he was suppressed [with grief]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and as-Suddi said: "meaning, he was distressed." 'Ata al-Khurasani and Abu Malik said: "meaning, he was afflicted."

We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said, ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, the words rose up and encircled the Throne. The angels said: "O Lord, this is a weak voice coming from a strange land, and it is recognizable." Allah said: "Do you not recognize it?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Yunus." They said: "O Lord, your servant whose good deeds have always been raised for him and whose supplications are answered?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, so that You rescue him from affliction?" So Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the open shore. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not appropriate for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri [[Al-Musnad (1/390) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4603).]], and it is in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4631) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2376).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿would slip you﴾ means they would pierce you with their eyes, that is, they would harm you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you out of their hatred for you, were it not for Allah's protection of you and His guarding of you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye ('ayn) is real and has real effect, by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as numerous hadiths have been related through many different chains confirming this.

The hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us (ḥ). And al-'Abbas al-'Anbari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Sharik informed us, from al-'Abbas ibn Dhurayh, from ash-Sha'bi, (al-'Abbas said: from Anas), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah (incantation for healing) except for the evil eye, or a sting, or bleeding that does not stop." Al-'Abbas did not mention the evil eye. This is the wording of Sulayman [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3889).]].

The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu 'Abdullah Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far ar-Razi, from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a sting" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3513).]].

Thus Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Husayn ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion), and it contains a story [[Sahih Muslim, no. (220).]]. Shu'bah also narrated it from Husayn, from ash-Sha'bi, from Buraydah, as at-Tirmidhi said [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi (4/345).]]. Al-Imam al-Bukhari narrated this hadith through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, Abu Dawud through the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal, and at-Tirmidhi through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. All three narrated it from Husayn, from 'Amir, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, as a mawquf [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5705); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3884); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2075).]].

The hadith of Abu Jundub ibn Junadah: The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah ibn al-Birind as-Sami narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Abi Dubay narrated to us, from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the evil eye causes a man to fall by the permission of Allah, so he rises up shaved (bald?), then falls down from it." Its isnad is gharib (rare), and they did not narrate it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of Abu Ya'la, but in it there is: Ibrahim, from Daylam, from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr, so Abu Harb is dropped. The explanation of that will come from Ibn 'Adi's words. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5/146) through the chain of Yunus ibn Muhammad, and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/104) through the chain of as-Salt ibn Mas'ud, both from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Wahb, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan, from Abu Dharr. Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is narrated by Daylam from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, and I think the error is in the narration of as-Salt, where he said: 'from Wahb ibn Abi Dubay, from Abu Harb, from Mihjan.' Perhaps Abu Harb is Mihjan."]].

The hadith of Habis at-Tamimi: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad narrated to us, Harb narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Hayyah ibn Habis at-Tamimi narrated to me, that his father informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no harm in the hamma (a type of vermin or a poisonous insect), the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen (al-fa'l)" [[Al-Musnad (5/70). In manuscript m: "al-tayr" (the omen), and in manuscript a: "al-zann" (the suspicion).]].

At-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from Abu Ghassan Yahya ibn Kathir, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with it. Then he said: "gharib." He said: Shayban narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah ibn Habis, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Hasan ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Shayban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hayyah, who narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no harm in the hamma, the evil eye is real, and the truest omen is the good omen" [[Al-Musnad (5/70).]].

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Duwayd, Isma'il ibn Thawban narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real, it brings down the one who is shaved (bald?)" [[Al-Musnad (1/274).]]. Gharib.

Another chain: Muslim said in his Sahih: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the decree, the evil eye would have preceded it. And when you are asked to wash (from the evil eye), then wash." Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2188).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: "I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every envious evil eye." And he said: "Thus Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ishaq and Isma'il, peace be upon them."

Al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of al-Minhal, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3371); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4737); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2060); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10844); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3525).]].

The hadith of Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: 'I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as delicate as a hidden maiden's.' Shortly afterward, Sahl was struck down, and he was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was said to him: 'Attend to Sahl, he has fallen.' He said: 'Whom do you suspect of this?' They said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah.' He said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? When one of you sees in his brother something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing for him.' Then he called for water and commanded 'Amir to perform ablution, washing his face, his two hands up to the elbows, his two knees, and the inner part of his waist-wrap, and he commanded that the water be poured over him."

Sufyan said: Ma'mar said, from az-Zuhri: "And he commanded that the vessel be overturned from behind him" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3509).]].

An-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both from az-Zuhri, with it. And through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah also, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah: "and the vessel is overturned from behind him." And through the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, with it. And through the hadith of Malik also, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, with it [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7617–7619).]].

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eyes of the jinn and the evil eyes of mankind. When al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two surahs of the Qur'an) were revealed, he took hold of them and left aside whatever else.

At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Sa'id ibn Iyas Abu Mas'ud al-Jurayri, with it [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3511); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (2058); Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/271).]]. At-Tirmidhi said: "hasan" (good).

Another hadith from him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to me, Abu Nadrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, have you been unwell?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and every eye, may He heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you" [[Al-Musnad (3/28).]].

He narrated it also from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Warith, the same. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/56); Sahih Muslim, no. (2186); Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (975); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (10843); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3523).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, or Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and Jibril came to him and said: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from every envious person and evil eye, and may Allah heal you" [[Al-Musnad (3/75).]].

He also narrated it through Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman at-Tufawi, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, with it [[Al-Musnad (3/58).]].

Abu Zur'ah ar-Razi said: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated from his father, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Abu Nadrah, and from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are sahih (sound).

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Indeed, the evil eye is real'" [[Al-Musnad (2/318).]].

They (al-Bukhari and Muslim) both narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2187).]].

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Mudarib ibn Hazn, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with the same wording. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3507, and al-Musnad (2/487).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Thawr (meaning Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, from Makhul, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real, and the devil attends it, and the envy of the son of Adam." [[al-Musnad (2/439).]]

Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurayrah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah say, "Bad omen is in three: the house, the horse and the woman"? He said: I said: Then I would be attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something he did not say! Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of omens is good omen (fa'l), and the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (2/289).]]

The hadith of Asma' bint 'Umays: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, who said: Asma' said: O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye; shall I seek a remedy (istirqa') for them? He said: "Yes. For if anything could outstrip the decree (qadr), the evil eye would have outstripped it." [[Ibid.]]

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. [[al-Musnad (6/438); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]] Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Urwah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from Asma' bint 'Umays, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2059; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7537.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

The hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Ibn Majah said: 'Ali ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to seek a remedy (istirqa') for the evil eye. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3510.]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, with the same chain. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan and Mis'ar, both from Ma'bad, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5738; Sahih Muslim, no. 2195.]]

Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Waqid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek refuge in Allah, for the soul (nafs) is real." He alone narrated it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3508. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/134): "In this chain there is some weakness (maqal)."]]

Abu Dawud said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The one who had caused the evil eye (al-'a'in) used to be commanded to perform ablution, and water from it would be washed over the one afflicted (al-ma'in). [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3880.]]

The hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways [[In M: "Abu Idris".]] narrated to us, al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and they travelled with him toward Makkah, until when they were at Shi'b al-Kharrar (from al-Juhfah), Sahl ibn Hunayf bathed, and he was a fair-skinned man of good build and complexion. 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b, saw him while he was bathing and said: "I have never seen anything like today, nor skin so concealed (jild mukhabba'ah)!" Sahl then collapsed (lubit). He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, would you come to Sahl? By Allah, he cannot raise his head, and he does not regain consciousness." He said: "Do you suspect anyone of causing it?" They said: "'Amir ibn Rabi'ah looked at him." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Amir and rebuked him severely, saying: "Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not, when you saw something that pleased you, invoke blessing (barak)?" Then he said to him: "Bathe for him." So 'Amir washed his face, his two hands, his two elbows, his two knees, the tips of his two feet and the inner edge of his waist-wrap in a vessel, and then that water was poured over him, poured by a man over his head and back from behind, and then the vessel was overturned behind him. He did this, and Sahl went out with the people, with no harm in him. [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of 'Amir: Waki' narrated to us, my father (Waki's father) narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Hind ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf set out wanting to bathe. He said: They went seeking a place with a covering (al-khamr) for bathing. He said: 'Amir put down a woollen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and struck him with my eye (fa-asabtuhu bi-'aynī), and he went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling (far'qa) from him in the water, so I came to him and called to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: Then he came walking and entered the water, as if I were looking at the whiteness of his shins. He said: Then he struck his chest with his hand and said: "O Allah, turn away from him its heat, its cold and its affliction (wasab)." He said: Then he stood up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When any of you sees in his brother, or in himself, or in his property, something that pleases him, let him invoke blessing (fal-yubarrik), for the evil eye is real." [[al-Musnad (3/486).]]

The hadith of Jabir: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl al-Ansari narrated to us, he is called Ibn al-Daji', the companion (daji') of Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Most of my ummah die after the Book of Allah, His decree and His divine decree (qadr), by way of souls (bi-al-anfus)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3052 (Kashf al-Astar); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/106): "Its narrators are the narrators of the sahih, except Talib ibn Habib ibn 'Amr, who is trustworthy (thiqah)."]]

Al-Bazzar said: He means the evil eye. He said: We do not know this hadith to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this chain.

I say: Rather, it has been narrated by another route from Jabir. The hafiz Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Munthir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned it in his book al-'Aja'ib, which contains noble and strange benefits: Al-Rahawi narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real; it brings a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot. Indeed, most of the destruction of my ummah is from the evil eye." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/185) through Rahim, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali al-Lahbi, with the same wording, and said: [not preserved (ghayr mahfuz)]. 'Ali ibn Abi 'Ali is weak (afanah); Ahmad said: he narrates unfamiliar (munkar) hadiths from Jabir.]]

Then he narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye may bring a man into the grave, and bring a camel into the cooking pot." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/408), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/90), through several routes from Shu'ayb ibn Ayyub with the same wording. Abu Nu'aym said: "Strange from the hadith of al-Thawri; Mu'awiyah alone narrated it." Ibn 'Adi said the same.]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Hisham ibn Abi Ruqayyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion ('adwa), no bad omen (tiyarah), no hamah, and no envy (hasad), and the evil eye is real." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[al-Musnad (2/222).]]

A hadith from 'Ali: The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Khaythamah ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Kashuri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Basri narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him distressed, and said: "O Muhammad, what is this distress I see in your face?" He said: "Al-Hasan and al-Husayn have been afflicted by the evil eye." He said: "The evil eye has spoken the truth, for the evil eye is real. Why did you not seek refuge (ta'awwadhta) for them with these words?" He said: "And what are they, O Jibril?" He said: Say: "O Allah, Lord of the great authority, possessor of ancient favour, possessor of the noble face, Guardian of the perfect words and the answered supplications, heal al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind." So the Prophet ﷺ said it, and they both got up playing before him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek refuge for yourselves, your women and your children with this charm (ta'widh), for those who seek refuge have never sought refuge with its like."

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Hayati alone narrated it, from the people of Tustar. [[In Tarikh Dimashq: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hanzali", and in Kanz al-'Ummal: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khatibi"; I have not determined the correct form, and Allah knows best.]] Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in the biography of "Tarrad ibn al-Husayn" in his Tarikh. [[Tarikh Dimashq (8/503, manuscript).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, they belittle him with their eyes and harm him with their tongues, and they say: ﴿Indeed, he is mad﴾, because of his bringing the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾
